author: ryanklee
body:
## Summary

4-batch performance optimization for hapax-logos, addressing latent hazards identified during analysis:

### Batch 1: Quick Wins
- **Unified VL polling**: Remove `useVisualLayerPoll()` manual poll hook. All consumers share a single react-query `useVisualLayer()` cache (2s refetch). Eliminates duplicate requests.
- **Region memoization**: All 5 terrain regions wrapped in `React.memo()`.
- **DetectionOverlay visibility gate**: Skip canvas rAF when container is off-screen via `offsetParent` check.
- **smoothedRef Map cap**: Safety valve at 200 entries prevents unbounded growth.

### Batch 2: Context Split — ClassificationOverlayContext → 3 Contexts
- **SignalContext**: perception, visualLayer, filteredSignals, signalsByRegion, stimmungStance (~2s change rate)
- **DetectionContext**: classificationDetections, detection visibility/tier (~2s + user toggles)
- **OverlayControlContext**: overlayMode, channelVisibility, zoneOpacityOverrides (user interaction only)
- All 10 consumers updated to narrowest context. `useOverlay()` remains as convenience.

### Batch 3: TerrainContext Split
- **TerrainDisplayContext**: focusedRegion, regionDepths, activeOverlay, etc. (drives grid layout)
- **TerrainActionContext**: focusRegion, setRegionDepth, cycleDepth, etc. (stable callbacks)
- GroundRegion and TerrainPage use actions-only, avoiding re-renders on display changes.

### Batch 4: Snapshot Polling
- `useSnapshotPoll` gains `enabled` parameter for depth-aware polling control.
- Backend VL endpoint split deferred (optional, lower priority).

## Test plan
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `vite build` succeeds
- [ ] Navigate all terrain depths — camera feeds work, detection halos visible
- [ ] Press S → DetailPane controls work
- [ ] React DevTools Profiler: rapid G presses — only focused region re-renders
- [ ] React DevTools Profiler: toggle detectionTier — only overlays re-render, not regions
- [ ] Network tab: single polling endpoint for visual-layer, ~1 req/2s

author: copilot
body:
Several text-over-image areas fail WCAG AA contrast requirements — notably `text-white/40` on gallery cards and `text-white/50` on featured cards, plus weak gradient overlays that can't guarantee readability on bright images.

### Changes

- **Reusable contrast utilities** (`globals.css`): `.text-on-image` (multi-layer `text-shadow`) and `.text-on-image-backdrop` (`backdrop-filter: brightness(0.7)`) for adaptive darkening behind text regardless of image content
- **User preference media queries**: `prefers-contrast: more` strengthens shadows and overlays; `prefers-reduced-transparency` makes overlays near-opaque
- **Gradient strengthening**: hero `from-black/60→70`, `via-black/10→20`; featured cards `from-black/50→60`; gallery cards `from-black/60→70`
- **Text opacity fixes**: `text-white/40→70`, `text-white/50→70`, `text-white/80→90` across all overlay text

```css
/* Adaptive darkening — works regardless of underlying image brightness */
.text-on-image {
  text-shadow: 0 1px 3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.6), 0 2px 8px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35);
}
.text-on-image-backdrop {
  backdrop-filter: brightness(0.7) saturate(1.1);
}

@media (prefers-contrast: more) {
  .image-gradient-overlay {
    --tw-gradient-from: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.85) var(--tw-gradient-from-position);
  }
}
```

author: wentingchua
body:
### What changed

**user-service**: added isAdmin to the JWT payload on login, shortened token expiry from 1d to 15m
**question-service**: AdminGuard now verifies the JWT locally using JWT_SECRET instead of calling user-service's /auth/verify-token endpoint

### Why
Previously, every admin-guarded request in question-service made a network call to user-service to validate the token. This creates an unnecessary dependency — if user-service is down, question-service can't authenticate anyone.
By embedding isAdmin in the JWT and verifying it locally, question-service can authenticate requests independently.

### Testing

Valid admin token → 200 (In postman, try `POST http://localhost:3002/questions` using admin token)
Valid non-admin token → 403 (In postman, try `POST http://localhost:3002/questions` using non-admin user token)
Missing/malformed token → 401 (In postman, try `POST http://localhost:3002/questions` without token input)

author: copilot
body:
Adds an audit rule that requires `ALTER TABLE` to specify an `ALGORITHM` clause, with an optional allowlist of accepted algorithms. Applies **only to MySQL 8.0+**. The `SupportAlterAlgorithm` config is validated at check time — any value outside `{DEFAULT, INPLACE, COPY, INSTANT}` is a hard error.

## New config (`[inc]`)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `check_alter_algorithm` | bool | `false` | Require `ALGORITHM=` on all `ALTER TABLE` |
| `support_alter_algorithm` | string | `""` | Comma-separated allowlist; empty = any of the 4 valid values accepted |

## New error codes

| Code | Level | Message |
|------|-------|---------|
| `ErrAlterTableAlgorithmRequired` | 1 (warn) | No `ALGORITHM` clause found |
| `ErrAlterTableAlgorithmNotSupport` | 1 (warn) | Specified algorithm not in allowlist |
| `ErrAlterTableAlgorithmInvalidConfig` | 2 (error) | `support_alter_algorithm` contains a value outside `DEFAULT/INPLACE/COPY/INSTANT` |

## Behavior

```sql
-- check_alter_algorithm = true, support_alter_algorithm = "INPLACE,INSTANT"

ALTER TABLE t1 ADD COLUMN c1 INT;
-- ✗ ErrAlterTableAlgorithmRequired

ALTER TABLE t1 ADD COLUMN c1 INT, ALGORITHM=COPY;
-- ✗ ErrAlterTableAlgorithmNotSupport: 'COPY' not in 'INPLACE,INSTANT'

ALTER TABLE t1 ADD COLUMN c1 INT, ALGORITHM=INPLACE;
-- ✓ OK
```

If `support_alter_algorithm = "INPLACE,BADVAL"`, `ErrAlterTableAlgorithmInvalidConfig` fires for `BADVAL` before any statement check runs. The entire feature is a no-op on MySQL < 8.0, MariaDB, TiDB, and OceanBase.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## 需求

在 ALTER TABLE 语句审核中增加一个规则：**必须指定 ALGORITHM 子句**，并且可以通过配置项限定允许使用的算法类型（如 INPLACE、COPY、INSTANT）。

## 背景

目前在 `session/session_inception.go` 的 `checkAlterTable` 方法中，对 `ast.AlterTableAlgorithm` 类型的 spec 只做了"不做校验，允许这些参数"的处理（约第 3602-3607 行）：

```go
case ast.AlterTableLock,
    ast.AlterTableAlgorithm,
    ast.AlterTableForce:
    // 不做校验,允许这些参数
```

## 需要修改的内容

### 1. `config/config.go` - 在 `Inc` 结构体中增加两个配置项

```go
// 是否检查 ALTER TABLE 必须指定 ALGORITHM（默认 false）
CheckAlterAlgorithm bool `toml:"check_alter_algorithm" json:"check_alter_algorithm"`

// 允许的 DDL ALGORITHM 列表，多个以逗号分隔。为空时不限制具体算法（只要求指定即可）
// 可选值: INPLACE, COPY, INSTANT
SupportAlterAlgorithm string `toml:"support_alter_algorithm" json:"support_alter_algorithm"`
```

### 2. `session/errors.go` - 新增两个错误码

在 `ER_ERROR_LAST` 之前（`ER_TOOL_BASED_UNIQUE_INDEX_WARNING` 之前）新增：

```go
ErrAlterTableAlgorithmRequired   // ALTER TABLE 必须指定 ALGORITHM
ErrAlterTableAlgorithmNotSupport // 指定的 ALGORITHM 不在允许列表中
```

在 `ErrorsDefault` map 中增加对应的英文错误消息：

```go
ErrAlterTableAlgorithmRequired:   "ALTER TABLE must specify ALGORITHM clause.",
ErrAlterTableAlgorithmNotSupport: "ALTER TABLE ALGORITHM '%s' is not allowed. Supported algorithms: '%s'.",
```

在 `ErrorsChinese` map 中增加对应的中文错误消息：

```go
ErrAlterTableAlgorithmRequired:   "ALTER TABLE 必须指定 ALGORITHM 子句.",
ErrAlterTableAlgorithmNotSupport: "ALTER TABLE 指定的 ALGORITHM '%s' 不被允许. 支持的算法: '%s'.",
```

### 3. `config/error_level.go` - 新增错误级别配置

在已有的 IncLevel 结构体中添加对应的 error level 字段：

```go
ErAlterTableAlgorithmRequired   uint8 `toml:"er_alter_table_algorithm_required" json:"er_alter_table_algorithm_required"`
ErAlterTableAlgorithmNotSupport uint8 `toml:"er_alter_table_algorithm_not_support" json:"er_alter_table_algorithm_not_support"`
```

同时在初始化默认值的位置设置默认级别为 1（warning）或按照已有模式设置。

### 4. `session/session_inception.go` - 在 `checkAlterTable` 中增加检查逻辑

在 `checkAlterTable` 方法中，当 `s.inc.CheckAlterAlgorithm` 为 `true` 时：

1. 遍历 `node.Specs`，检查是否有 `ast.AlterTableAlgorithm` 类型的 spec
2. 如果没有找到，则报错 `ErrAlterTableAlgorithmRequired`
3. 如果找到了��且 `s.inc.SupportAlterAlgorithm` 不为空，则检查指定的 ALGORITHM 值是否在允许列表中
4. 如果不在允许列表中，则报错 `ErrAlterTableAlgorithmNotSupport`

需要注意的实现细节：
- `ast.AlterTableSpec` 中有 `Algorithm` 字段，类型为 `ast.AlgorithmType`，取值有 `AlgorithmTypeDefault(0)`, `AlgorithmTypeCopy(1)`, `AlgorithmTypeInplace(2)`, `AlgorithmTypeInstant(3)`
- `SupportAlterAlgorithm` 配置值类似于 `"INPLACE,COPY"`，需要拆分后与 `AlgorithmType.String()` 的返回值（如 "INPLACE", "COPY", "INSTANT"）做大小写不敏感比较
- 如果用户指定了 `ALGORITHM=DEFAULT`，需要根据需要决定是否允许（建议：如果配置了允许列表但不包含 DEFAULT，则报错）

建议在 `checkAlterTable` 方法中，在现有的 `for i, alter := range node.Specs` 循环之前添加算法检查：

```go
if s.inc.CheckAlterAlgorithm {
    hasAlgorithm := false
    var algorithmValue ast.AlgorithmType
    for _, alter := range node.Specs {
        if alter.Tp == ast.AlterTableAlgorithm {
            hasAlgorithm = true
            algorithmValue = alter.Algorithm
            break
        }
    }
    if !hasAlgorithm {
        s.appendErrorNo(ErrAlterTableAlgorithmRequired)
    } else if s.inc.SupportAlterAlgorithm != "" {
        supportAlgorithms := strings.Split(s.inc.SupportAlterAlgorithm, ",")
        found := false
        algStr := algorithmValue.String()
        for _, sa := range supportAlgorithms {
            if strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(sa), algStr) {
                found = true
                break
            }
        }
        if !found {
            s.appendErrorNo(ErrAlterTableAlgorithmNotSupport, algStr, s.inc.SupportAlterAlgorithm)
        }
    }
}
```

### 5. `config/config.toml.default` - 增加默认配置说明

在 `[inc]` section 中增加：

```toml
# 是否检查 ALTER TABLE 必须指定 ALGORITHM
check_alter_algorithm = false

# 允许的 ALTER TABLE ALGORITHM 列表，多个以逗号分隔，为空时不限制
# 可选值: INPLACE, COPY, INSTANT
support_alter_algorithm = ""
```

### 6. 测试

在 `session/session_inception_test.go` 中添加测试用例，验证：
- 开启 `check_alter_algorithm` 后，不指定 ALGORITHM 的 ALTER TABLE 语句报错
- 指定了 ALGORITHM=INPLACE 且在允许列表中时通过
- 指定了 ALGORITHM=COPY 但不在允许列表中时报错
- 不开启 `check_alter_algorithm` 时不做检查

body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a comprehensive quality control (QC) audit system for AI-generated review replies, along with enhanced prompt instructions to prevent common issues like technician number fabrication, placeholder leakage, and information hallucination.

## Key Changes

- **QC Audit System**: Added `check_reply_quality()` function that validates AI-generated replies against 7 strict criteria:
  - Technician number fabrication detection
  - Placeholder/template variable residue checking
  - Unsupported product recommendation validation
  - Conditional sentence detection
  - Star rating tone matching
  - Information fabrication detection
  - Reply length validation

- **Enhanced Prompt Instructions**: Updated `PROMPT_TEMPLATE` with:
  - New rule against example leakage (rule #5)
  - Clarified handling of "technician" mentions without specific numbers
  - Additional validation checklist item for technician number verification
  - New example (Example 4) demonstrating correct handling of technician mentions without numbers

- **QC System Prompt**: Added `QC_SYSTEM_PROMPT` and `QC_PROMPT_TEMPLATE` that instruct the AI to perform strict JSON-formatted audits with detailed reasoning for each check

- **Integration**: Modified `process_single_task()` to call QC audit after AI reply generation, with automatic fallback to original reply if audit fails

- **API Updates**: 
  - Updated default model from `glm-4-flash` to `glm-4.7-flash`
  - Added 429 rate limit handling with exponential backoff retry

- **Dependencies**: Added `json` and `re` imports for QC response parsing

- **Gitignore**: Added `__pycache__/` to version control

## Implementation Details

The QC audit returns a JSON response with:
- `passed`: boolean indicating if all checks passed
- `checks`: array of 7 validation results with detailed explanations
- `fixed_reply`: corrected reply if issues were found, otherwise null

The system uses regex to extract JSON from potential markdown code blocks in the QC response, ensuring robust parsing. If QC fails but provides a corrected reply, that corrected version is used; otherwise the original reply is retained with a warning logged.

body:
Three root causes of duplicate/spam notifications fixed:

1. cell_reference used row_idx (Сегодня!B{row}:{date}) which breaks when rows shift in Google Sheets. Changed to subject-based key (Сегодня!{subject}:{date}) — same grade won't be detected twice even if rows are inserted/deleted.

2. Morning flush (_flush_quiet_hours_queue) was dumping raw queued HTML messages as-is — no deduplication, no aggregation. Rewritten to query grade_history directly, group by student, deduplicate by subject, and produce a clean compact summary with avg scores. Falls back to raw queue for non-grade notifications (quarters etc).

3. Updated i18n: "уведомлений" → "оценок" in morning header (ru/en/uz) to match the new aggregated format.

Before (6 messages for 4 grades):
  🌅 За ночь поступило 6 уведомлений:
  ✏️ Англ 5→4 | ⚠️ Геометрия 3 | 👍 Анатомия 4 | 👍 Англ 4
  👍 3 оценок: Англ 4, Геом 3, Анат 4 | 👍 Англ 4  ← duplicates

After (1 message for 4 grades):

  👨‍🎓 Заур: Англ 4, Геом 3, Анат 4 (ср: 3.7)

body:
SCMI allows platform firmware to deliver Platform-to-Agent (P2A) notifications
to the agent via the RX transport channel.

These notifications share the same interrupt signalling
mechanism as TX replies and must therefore be identified
and dispatched by inspecting the SCMI message header.

This PR introduces SCMI core support for:

  - decoding SCMI message headers
  - validating incoming message type
  - routing NOTIFICATION messages to protocol handlers
  - protocol-level static registration of event callbacks

Transport drivers are now required to pass the received
message header to the core via the transport callback
to allow notification-aware dispatch.

body:
This PR adds a comprehensive teaching implementation of the "Kth Smallest Element in a BST" problem (LeetCode #230) to the trees module.

It provides three distinct approaches:
1. **Brute Force:** In-order traversal to collect all nodes into a vector.
2. **Optimized:** Recursive in-order traversal tracking a counter state and returning early.
3. **Optimal:** Iterative in-order traversal using a `Vec` as an explicit stack to bypass call-stack limitations.

Key highlights:
- Proper use of `Option<&TreeNode>` via `as_deref()` to avoid ownership transfer.
- Explicit recursive state tracking using `&mut`.
- 100% test coverage covering happy paths, edge cases, and consistency checks across implementations.
- Full compliance with `clippy::pedantic` and `clippy::nursery` lints.

author: xroche
body:
## Summary

Install rules used a `ddprof/` prefix on all destinations, producing
paths like `<prefix>/ddprof/bin/ddprof` instead of the standard
`<prefix>/bin/ddprof`. This breaks `cmake --install`, `find_package()`,
and Conan's `cmake.install()` without manual file relocation.

The [GNUInstallDirs](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/module/GNUInstallDirs.html)
convention expects `CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX` to control the top-level
directory, with `bin/`, `lib/`, `include/` directly underneath.

## How

Remove the `ddprof/` prefix from install destinations and let
`CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX` control the layout. Update `setup_env.sh` to
append `/ddprof` to the install prefix so the release tarball keeps
the same `ddprof/bin/ddprof` structure.

License files now install to `licenses/` instead of the root.

body:
### Motivation
- Close gaps between service behaviour and the exposed API surface for Attendance and Leave so workflows can be exercised end-to-end. 
- Prevent invalid state transitions by ensuring incomplete/captured attendance cannot be approved without validation. 
- Expose period-level and observability endpoints (summary, absence alerts, locking) so higher-level UI and automation can rely on the API. 

### Description
- Added attendance API handlers in `attendance_service/api.py` for single-record fetch (`get_attendance_record`), approval (`post_attendance_approval`), period lock (`post_attendance_period_lock`), period summary (`get_attendance_summary`), and absence alerts (`get_attendance_absence_alerts`) and extended the API error mapping for the new error codes. 
- Hardened the approval flow in `attendance_service/service.py` so `approve_record` now raises `APPROVAL_REQUIRES_VALIDATED` unless the record is `Validated`. 
- Extended `leave_api.py` with handlers for submit (`post_leave_submit`), single-request fetch (`get_leave_request`) and patch/cancel (`patch_leave_request`), and thread-safe idempotency keys were wired through the API layer where appropriate. 
- Added/updated tests in `tests/test_attendance_service.py` and `tests/test_leave_api.py` to cover the newly exposed attendance endpoints and the invalid approval transition as well as the leave submit/get/cancel API flows. 

### Testing
- Ran the full targeted test set with `pytest tests/test_attendance_service.py tests/unit/test_attendance_api_standards.py tests/test_leave_service.py tests/test_leave_api.py tests/api/test_gateway_api_standards.py tests/test_api_gateway_routes.py -q` and all tests passed. 
- Final run result: `46 passed, 26 subtests passed` indicating the new endpoints and approval guard are covered and stable.

body:
## Summary
This PR adds support for displaying speech bubbles from the player character and implements click-away dismissal for all speech bubbles in the game scene.

## Key Changes

- **Player Speech Bubbles**: Added `PlayerPositionPayload` event type and `PLAYER_POSITION_UPDATE` event to track player position, enabling speech bubbles to be displayed at the player's location when they send messages
- **Position Tracking**: Modified `HomeScene` to emit player position updates alongside existing Syzygy position updates, with proper canvas scaling calculations
- **Click-Away Dismissal**: Implemented a new `useEffect` hook in `GameModeShell` that listens for pointer events and dismisses bubbles when clicking outside of the bubble UI or input bar
- **Bubble Variant Styling**: Added `variant` prop to `SpeechBubbleOverlay` to support different visual styles for player vs NPC bubbles, with new CSS styling for player bubbles (blue gradient background)
- **Simplified Bubble Lifecycle**: Removed automatic dismissal timer logic from `SpeechBubbleStack` component, delegating all dismissal control to the parent component
- **State Management**: Added `playerBubbleText`, `playerPos`, and `sceneBubblesVisibleRef` to track player bubble state and visibility

## Implementation Details

- Player bubbles display immediately when the user sends a message, while NPC bubbles continue to appear after the API response
- Click-away detection uses `pointerdown` events and checks for specific CSS classes (`.game-bubble-input-bar`, `.speech-bubble-overlay`) to prevent accidental dismissal during interaction
- Player bubble styling uses a blue color scheme to visually distinguish it from NPC responses
- Position updates are emitted on scene resize to maintain accurate bubble positioning

### Motivation
- Grouped book filtering could match impossible combinations when different copies in a group satisfied different predicates (language, page count, availability) instead of requiring a single copy to satisfy all active filters.  
- The grouped filters and tests referenced `pageRange` in places where the UI uses `pageLimit`, causing incorrect behavior and a test-time reference error.  

### Description
- Update `matchesCopyFilters` in `public/app.js` to evaluate `language`, `pageLimit`, and `availability` against the same candidate copy so a group only matches if one copy satisfies all predicates.  
- Normalize and accept `pageLimit` in `matchesCopyFilters` and replace the prior `pageRange` call-site with `pageLimit` in `filterBooks` so the active UI field is used.  
- Use `matchesPageLimit` with the candidate's page count when evaluating page filters, removing reliance on an undefined `pageRange` variable.  
- Extend `tests/grouped-filters.test.js` to cover `pageLimit` cases and combined language/page and language/availability scenarios so mixed-copy matches are rejected and single-copy matches are preserved.

author: seakee
body:
## Summary
Harden PostgreSQL code generation around identifier selection and unsupported schema handling.

## Cause
The generator mixed explicit primary-key metadata with implicit prioritized fields.
That made different code paths disagree on the record identifier and introduced unsafe fallbacks for unsupported PostgreSQL schemas.

## Solution
- unify model and repository generation around a safe single-identifier path
- keep implicit `id` behavior for legacy and identity-backed tables in generated `Create`, `Last`, `Updates`, and `ListByArgs`
- reject repository generation for composite primary keys and tables without a safe single identifier
- prevent PostgreSQL `varchar[]` and `character varying[]` columns from being generated as scalar `string` fields
- add regression tests and generated-code format checks for implicit ids, composite keys, missing identifiers, and PostgreSQL array fallbacks

## Testing
- `go test -mod=mod ./command/codegen/codegen`

author: themavik
body:
## Summary
Fixes #26453.

**Root cause:** When OAuth2 token refresh fails (e.g. Microsoft Outlook after ~1 hour), the resulting error object may have an `undefined` `.stack` property. Downstream code that assigns or calls methods on `.stack` (like `.replace()` or `.split()`) throws `TypeError: dummy.stack.replace is not a function`, masking the real OAuth error.

**Fix:** Added nullish coalescing (`?? ''`) guards on three `.stack` assignment sites, and a `typeof` check before calling `.split()` on `error.stack`.

## Changes
- `packages/workflow/src/errors/workflow-activation.error.ts`: Guard `cause.stack` with `?? ''`
- `packages/core/src/execution-engine/workflow-execute.ts`: Guard `runExecutionData.resultData.error.stack` with `?? ''`
- `packages/workflow/src/utils.ts`: Add `typeof error.stack === 'string'` check before calling `.split()`

## Testing
- Verified fix prevents TypeError when error.stack is undefined
- Change is minimal (3 lines) and backward-compatible
- No behavioral change when error.stack is a valid string

author: copilot
body:
Active sessions were surfacing failures as plain text banners, regardless of whether the problem was transient, auth/billing-related, or a hard context limit. This change threads structured error metadata from the session manager through SSE to the client so the session page can render recovery actions that match the failure mode. - **Structured error contract** - Added a shared `SessionErrorInfo` shape with: - `message` - `category` - `recoverable` - Updated active-session init/error SSE payloads to carry structured errors instead of plain strings. - **Server-side error categorization** - Classified SDK/session failures in `session-manager.ts` into actionable categories: - `authentication` - `billing` - `rate_limit` - `context_limit` - `transient` - `action` / `network` where appropriate - Used SDK-native signals where available: - assistant errors like `authentication_failed` / `billing_error` - result subtypes like `error_max_turns` - Preserved existing session replay/init behavior while making the last error available as structured state. - **Recovery-oriented session UI** - Added `ErrorBanner.svelte` as a compact alert strip (warning icon + bold category label + message on one line, underlined text links for actions) — intentionally distinct from message-thread elements to avoid visual confusion. - Replaced generic session error rendering with category-specific recovery actions: - **Retry last prompt** (underlined link with loading spinner) for recoverable/transient/rate-limit/action failures - **Open Settings** (underlined link) for auth/billing failures - **Start new session** (accent-colored underlined link) for context overflow / max-turn failures - Kept resume/start errors in the same structured format so they render consistently. - **Non-blocking network failure handling** - Changed transient client-side fetch/connection failures to show as dismissable toast-style notices with wifi icon, title/subtitle layout, and close button — instead of overwriting the persistent session error state. - Added `retryLastPrompt()` to the active-session client so recovery can re-send the last prompt after crashes/disconnects. - **Project-scoped recovery flow** - Extended the existing new-session modal store so recovery actions can open the modal preselected to the current project. Example of the new error contract: ```ts type SessionErrorInfo = { message: string; category: | 'transient' | 'authentication' | 'billing' | 'context_limit' | 'action' | 'network' | 'rate_limit' | 'unknown'; recoverable: boolean; }; ``` ## Screenshots ### Home screen (unchanged) ![Home screen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0a589b8a-3ba2-49bb-a632-522cbbe36e44) ### Search view (unchanged) ![Search view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9556474d-8065-4eba-b44d-646d311d4b94) ### Error: Recoverable / Transient — "Retry last prompt" link ![Transient error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4fbd2b1f-3813-4d0b-a3ad-442f4810f8d3) ### Error: Authentication — "Open Settings" link ![Auth error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3259cb74-7580-4f66-be45-0bb432d8f0fd) ### Error: Context Limit — "Start new session" link (accent color) ![Context limit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e931ae8-2e4d-4ccd-bcb9-9469f8e7ee8e) ### Error: Billing — "Open Settings" link ![Billing error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c65214ce-0781-4c76-abd8-095b4b371b33) ### Error: Rate Limited — "Retry last prompt" link ![Rate limit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6846baa6-c700-42cc-975d-908dcf2a8600) ### Network toast — dismissable connection notice ![Network toast](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1c902e83-8f8d-467f-9542-c74862e6a976) ### Live runtime error — real error with retry action ![Live error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/90762bfd-9328-43f7-b03e-d03fb4d3247a)
Original prompt > > ---- > > *This section details on the original issue you should resolve* > > Structured error recovery UI for active sessions > ## Problem > > Active sessions display errors as plain text banners with no actionable recovery options. When something goes wrong, the user sees a red text message but has no buttons to retry, reconfigure, or navigate to a fix. > > ### Current behavior > > The session page (`src/routes/session/[projectId]/[sessionId]/+page.svelte`, lines 216–230) renders two basic error banners: > > ```svelte > {#if session?.error} >
> {session.error} >
> {/if} > > {#if resumeError} >
> {resumeError} >
> {/if} > ``` > > The SSE store (`src/lib/stores/active-session.svelte.ts`) sets `error` as a plain string for several categories — rate limits, SSE connection loss, action failures, and SDK errors — but they all display identically. > > The server (`src/lib/server/session-manager.ts`) always broadcasts errors with `recoverable: true` and doesn't distinguish error categories (no checks for `authentication_failed`, `billing_error`, `error_max_turns`, or context overflow). > > ### What's missing > > From the [original implementation plan](https://github.com/DavidTeju/claude-inspector/blob/main/.claude/plans/async-pondering-pebble.md) (Phase 4c): > > 1. **"Retry" button** — Re-sends the last prompt to restart after a crash or transient failure > 2. **Auth error handling** — Detect `authentication_failed` / `billing_error` from the SDK and show "Configure API key in Settings" link pointing to `/settings` > 3. **Context overflow handling** — Detect context overflow (SDK exit code 1 or `error_max_turns` result subtype) and show "Start new session in this project" link > 4. **Toast notifications for network errors** — Non-blocking toasts for transient `fetch` failures (currently these overwrite the persistent `error` state, which clears on the next successful action) > 5. **Error categorization on the server** — `consumeQuery()` should inspect error types and set appropriate `recoverable` flags and error categories in the broadcast, so the client can render context-specific recovery actions > > ### Suggested approach > > - Add an `ErrorBanner.svelte` component (or enhance the inline banners) that accepts an error object with `{ message, category, recoverable }` and renders category-specific action buttons > - On the server, classify errors in `consumeQuery()` catch block and in result-message handling > - Consider existing issues DavidTeju/claude-inspector#40 (no error handling in settings save) and DavidTeju/claude-inspector#66 (stale errors not cleared on reconnect) which are related > > ## References > > - Plan: Phase 4c in `.claude/plans/async-pondering-pebble.md` > - Related: DavidTeju/claude-inspector#31 (Extract StatusBanner component), DavidTeju/claude-inspector#66 (stale error clearing) > > 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) > > ## Comments on the Issue (you are @copilot in this section) > > > >
- Fixes DavidTeju/claude-inspector#90 --- 💡 You can make Copilot smarter by setting up custom instructions, customizing its development environment and configuring Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. Learn more [Copilot coding agent tips](https://gh.io/copilot-coding-agent-tips) in the docs.

### Notification bell + center (`components/notifications/`)
- `NotificationBell` — bell icon with unread count badge, Supabase realtime subscription on `postgres_changes` for live insert events

### API routes

- `POST /api/push/subscribe` — upserts browser push subscription
- `POST /api/push/send` — sends via `web-push`, auto-cleans expired subscriptions (410/404)
- `POST /api/admin/send-notification` — batch processing (100/batch), supports in-app + push, all-users or specific targeting

### Pages
- `/notifications` — full list with all/unread filter tabs
- `/admin-fxk92p-sadab/notifications` — bulk send UI with recipient targeting, type selection, preview, delivery method toggles

### Settings integration (`app/settings/page.tsx`)
- New "Notifications" section with toggles for push, in-app, and per-type preferences

### Client libraries

body:
In debezium_ingestion mode with schema evolution enabled, the DorisSystemService

  single connection.

author: mcelb1200
body:
🚨 **Severity:** MEDIUM
💡 **Vulnerability:** Uninitialized Stack Memory Leak (Information Leak). In `src/umpProcessor.cpp`, arrays used to hold parsed string payloads (such as MIDI Endpoint Names and Lyrics) were only partially written if the parsed string was shorter than the array's maximum capacity. The remaining bytes contained stale stack data. When this array was passed to user callbacks, it exposed uninitialized memory to the application.
🎯 **Impact:** Exposing uninitialized stack memory can leak sensitive data from previous operations or cause unpredictable behavior in user callbacks that expect clean buffers.
🔧 **Fix:** Explicitly zero-initialized the `text[14]`, `text[13]`, and `text[12]` arrays (`uint8_t text[...] = {0};`) prior to sequential bitwise population.
✅ **Verification:** Compiled the C++ library with strict warnings (`-Wuninitialized`) and successfully ran the test suite (`159 tests passed, 0 failed`). Added a journal entry explaining the vulnerability.

body:
Dependabot was only running version update checks (monthly for Actions, weekly for npm) with no dedicated cadence for security vulnerabilities.

Adds `security-updates-only: true` blocks with `interval: daily` for both ecosystems, so security-advisory-driven PRs are raised daily. Existing version-update schedules are untouched.

```yaml
- package-ecosystem: "npm"
  directory: "/"
  schedule:
    interval: "daily"
  labels:
    - "dependencies"
    - "security"
  commit-message:
    prefix: "deps"
  open-pull-requests-limit: 10
```

author: xroche
body:
## Summary

When building ddprof as a dependency (Conan, FetchContent,
ExternalProject), the static analysis targets (cppcheck, clang-tidy,
format) are unnecessary overhead. They run configure-time tool lookups
and can fail if the tools aren't installed.

Following the pattern used by projects like
[abseil-cpp](https://github.com/abseil/abseil-cpp/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt)
which gate dev tooling behind options, this adds a
`DDPROF_ENABLE_STATIC_ANALYSIS` option so consumers can disable them.

## How

Wrap the `include(ClangTidy)`, `include(Format)`, and
`include(CppcheckConfig)` blocks in a single `if()` guard. Default is ON
so existing builds are unaffected. Consumers pass
`-DDDPROF_ENABLE_STATIC_ANALYSIS=OFF` to skip everything.

Also includes the `if(TARGET cppcheck)` guard from #1 for safety when
the option is ON but cppcheck isn't installed.

Multi-topic research on feature/researcher-7 branch:

### Abel-Ruffini (Inverse Galois Problem)
- **PROVED** `no_subgroup_order_15`: S₅ has no subgroup of order 15
  - Uses Sylow theory: unique normal Sylow 5- and 3-subgroups are disjoint

- Li's criterion (Li 1997, Bombieri-Lagarias 1999) as 10th equivalent formulation
- Equivalence network from K₉ (36 edges) to K₁₀ (45 edges)

- `Finite (Sylow p G)` is not automatically derived for finite groups in Mathlib;
  manually constructed via `Finite.of_injective SetLike.coe SetLike.coe_injective`
- `Subgroup.commute_of_normal_of_disjoint` is the cleanest path for order-pq abelianity

- **Updated Layout component** (`apps/scribe/scribe-react-common/src/components/Layout.tsx`):
  - Replaced simple "Sign out" button with a dropdown account menu
  - Menu includes links to the new account page and sign out action
  - Implements click-outside detection to close menu when clicking elsewhere

- **Enhanced TributaryContext** (`apps/scribe/scribe-react-common/src/context/tributaryContext.tsx`):
  - Added `AccountSession` interface to expose minimal session info (email)
  - Updated context to include `session` property

## Implementation Details

body:
Started from https://github.com/rh-ecosystem-edge/gori-lab/pull/290, that's commit c355c7a

author: gphuang
body:
## Summary

Closes #540, #541, #542, #543 (sub-issues of #516)

Adds CK grouped GEMM perf model mapping, perf models for MoE comm/causal conv1d/RoPE/CrossEntropy, and SSM categorization for ops found in Primus traces:

### #540 — CK grouped GEMM
- Maps `ck_grouped_gemm` and `ck_grouped_gemm_variable_k` to existing `primus_turbo_grouped_gemm` perf models (full GFLOPS + TB/s)

### #541 — SSM/Mamba ops
- `DaoAILab::_causal_conv1d_fwd_cpp` → **CausalConv1d perf model** (FLOPS = 2 × B × C × L × K, depthwise conv)
- `MambaSplitConv1dScanCombinedFn` → categorization-only as SSM_fwd/SSM_bwd (complex fused kernel, deferred to #552)

### #542 — MoE dispatch/combine
- **MoEComm perf model** for MoEDispatch/MoECombine: bytes = tokens × hidden × bpe, flops = 0 (pure communication)
- Auxiliary ops (TokenPermuteMaskMap, _OperationFuserAutogradFunction) → categorization-only
- Backward variants → categorization-only

### #543 — RoPE + CrossEntropy
- **FusedRoPE perf model** for FusedRoPEFunc: FLOPS = 3 × num_elements (6 ops per element pair), bytes = 2 × num_elements × bpe
- **CrossEntropy perf model** for CrossEntropyFunction: FLOPS ≈ 5 × batch × vocab_size, bytes = logits + targets + loss
- Backward variants → categorization-only

Models benefiting: Qwen3-8B, Mamba-370M, Zebra-Llama-1B, Kimi-K2

author: parasti
body:
Split the single build+deploy job into two separate jobs with independent concurrency groups:

- build: per-branch concurrency with cancel-in-progress=true, so rapid pushes to the same branch cancel stale builds (saves compute)
- deploy: single global concurrency group "pages" with cancel-in-progress=false, so deploys from different branches queue up and run one at a time instead of racing to force-push gh-pages

Built artifacts are passed between jobs via actions/upload-artifact / actions/download-artifact. PRs now build but skip deploy explicitly.

Main reason: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/99981/changes/57ea780f38d7383954935676eaee417b14d5fefe

Keywords like `if`, `for`, `while`, `else` were matched as bare substrings, causing false positives when they appear as part of identifiers (e.g. `DataLakeSpecific` contains `if`, `throwSomething` contains `throw`).

Add `\b` word boundaries around all keyword alternatives so only actual C++ keywords trigger the heuristic.

author: jonahgabriel
body:
## Problem

`infra-up` (and direct `docker compose up`) silently fails or produces cryptic errors when
required env vars are missing from `~/.omnibase/.env`. Docker Compose's `${VAR:?error}`
syntax aborts at startup, but there is no pre-flight check that surfaces missing vars before
the developer even attempts to start infra.

## Solution

Adds `scripts/check_required_env_vars.py` — a lightweight pre-commit guard that:

- Parses `docker/docker-compose.infra.yml` for `${VARNAME:?error}` required-var patterns
- Loads `~/.omnibase/.env`, considering only lines with a key and non-empty value
- Reports missing vars with exact remediation: `echo 'VAR=<set_me>' >> ~/.omnibase/.env`
- Exits 0 if all required vars are present, exits 1 if any are missing

The hook is registered in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with `files: docker/docker-compose\.infra\.yml`
so it fires whenever the compose file is modified, keeping the guard in sync as new required
vars are added.

## Files Changed

- `scripts/check_required_env_vars.py` — new script (argparse: `--compose-file`, `--env-file`)
- `.pre-commit-config.yaml` — adds `check-required-env-vars` hook to local hooks section

## Test Plan

- [x] `python scripts/check_required_env_vars.py` passes against local `~/.omnibase/.env`
- [x] All pre-commit hooks pass clean on commit
- [x] Script prints actionable remediation for each missing var

author: netlify-coding[bot]
body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/portfolio-thandolwethu-joni/agent-runs/69bbe09e1e0b85ecf181dfef

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** here is the error on admin still not fixed last chance

✅ **Result:** Fixed the admin section errors caused by two root issues: broken SPA routing and WebGL context leaks.

**SPA Routing (main fix):** The `netlify.toml` file was located at `src/dist/netlify.toml` instead of the project root, which meant Netlify never picked up the catch-all redirect rule (`/* → /index.html`). This caused all admin routes (`/admin`, `/admin/dashboard`, `/admin/create`, `/admin/edit/:slug`) to return a 404 error when accessed directly or refreshed in the browser. The file was moved to the project root and a `public/_redirects` fallback was also added for redundancy. The old misplaced file was removed.

**Three.js WebGL cleanup:** The `startLanding3D()` function created a new WebGL renderer, animation loop, and event listeners every time it was called, but never cleaned any of them up. Navigating between the Login page and Dashboard (both of which use the 3D background) would stack up multiple WebGL contexts, eventually hitting the browser's limit and causing a crash or blank screen. The function was refactored to automatically dispose of any previous instance before creating a new one, and all four components that use it (Login, Dashboard, Landing, GlobalBackground) now properly clean up on unmount via their `useEffect` return functions.

author: filiplajszczak
body:
`finalize()` previously mixed two concerns: platform configuration (`finalize_app_config`) and runtime mode setup (`test_mode`, `debugger`). This change moves runtime attributes to callers, so `finalize()` only handles host/tool verification and app config finalization.

With that separation in place, the `__draft__` magic attribute is replaced by a real class: `FinalizedAppConfig`. Unfinalized apps are `AppConfig`, finalized ones become `FinalizedAppConfig`. This would give the type checker a concrete type to track finalization state, replacing `hasattr`/`delattr` with `isinstance`.

Groundwork for typing app finalization (Refs #2739).

body:
Implements a futures trading market as a new financial instrument, allowing players to speculate on commodity price movements via long/short contracts with margin, locked-price settlement at expiry, and early close.

## Core System (`js/systems/finance/FuturesSystem.js`)
New module handling all futures logic:
- **Contract lifecycle**: `openLongContract` / `openShortContract` — deducts 20% margin, locks current market price, sets 10-day expiry
- **Settlement**: `advanceDay` auto-settles expired contracts; `closeContract` for early exit — both compute PnL as `(settlementPrice − lockedPrice) × unit × direction`
- **Portfolio state**: `getOpenContracts` (with live unrealized PnL), `getClosedContracts`, `getNetWorthAdjustment`
- Exposes `DEFAULT_TERM_DAYS` so UI can stay in sync without duplication

## State Schema (`js/data/constants.js`)
Two new v9 persisted fields:
```js
futuresContracts:        { type: 'array',  default: [] }
futuresLastProcessedDay: { type: 'number', default: 1  }
```

## Finance Integration (`js/systems/finance/FinanceSystem.js`)
- `Finance.init` delegates to `Futures.init`
- `Finance.advanceDay` delegates to `Futures.advanceDay`, merging log messages
- `getNetWorthAdjustment` adds futures unrealized PnL alongside stocks/investments/loans

## UI (`js/ui/TradeStationUI.js`)
Adds a **📋 期货市场** section to the 贸易站 tab:
- Per-commodity cards with current price, margin cost, held long/short count, and **做多/做空** buttons
- Open positions panel with unrealized PnL (color-coded) and **提前平仓** per contract
- Last 4 closed contracts summary

## Wiring (`js/core/GameManager.js`)
Three new handlers — `_handleFuturesLong`, `_handleFuturesShort`, `_handleFuturesClose` — passed into `TradeStationUI.render` via `financeActions`.

author: scriptraccoon
body: # Add Functors to CatDat As suggested in https://github.com/ScriptRaccoon/CatDat/issues/4, this PR adds functors, their properties, and implications of functor properties to CatDat. Several new tables and pages have been added. This PR also prepares for adding other categorical structures (such as monoidal categories or 2-categories) in the future. ## URLs In preparation for this PR, most of the old URLs for categories have been changed: `/search` has become `/category-search` and `/property/[id]` has become `/category-property/[id]`, etc. This has already been done in the main branch. This makes them consistent with the new URLs `/functor-search`, `/functor-property/[id]`, etc. ## Structure Selector The header has been redesigned. It now also includes a structure selector which allows to switch between categories and functors. It is also visible on mobile. The selected structure is defined by the URL. Switching to "functors" brings the user to the page with the list of functors and changes the navigation component (both on desktop and mobile appropriately: it now shows links to the functor pages. I have only added a few functors so far, more can be added later. For this reason there is also no search by name yet. ## Functor Detail Pages The functor detail page shows the definition of the functor, which includes source and target category, its satisfied and non-satisfied properties. As with categories, the application deduces further satisfied and non-satisfied properties by using implications (see below). ## Property List Page For now, I have added 27 properties of functors. We can add more later. Since there aren't so many, there is no search by name yet. ## Property Detail Page The property detail page shows the definition of a property of functors, its dual property (if available), relevant implications, functors that have this property, and functors that do not have this property. ## Deduction System As with categories and their properties, there is a script that automatically deduces properties of functors (satisfied or not) based on a list of implications. I have added the well-known implications between the existing properties. Implications are automatically dualized, e.g. `comonadic => left adjoint` is dualized from `monadic => right adjoint`. Again: since there aren't too many implications for now, there is no search yet. Also, there is no toggle to show/hide dualized implications (like on the page for category implications), the page just always shows all implications. As mentioned, the application deduces further satisfied and non-satisfied properties of functors by using these implications. ## Implication Detail Page As with implications between properties of categories, the implication detail page here shows the required assumptions of the functor and the conclusion(s), together with a proof or a reference to it. Here is the Special Adjoint Functor Theorem for example. There is a big difference to implications between properties of categories, though: As the example already shows, some results need assumptions also for the source or the target category. These need to be recorded as well. The deduction system uses these as well by checking the properties of the source and target categories that have been derived before. For example: when a functor with domain $\mathbf{FinSet}$ preserves products and equalizers, it is *not* deduced that it is continuous, since the result "product-preserving + equalizer-preserving => continuous" requires the domain to have products, and $\mathbf{FinSet}$ does not have products. However, it has *finite* products, so we can deduce at least that the functor is left exact. ## Search It is possible to search for functors that satisfy some properties while not satisfying others. This is basically the same as for categories. For example, one can search for functors that are cocontinuous but not continuous. ## Missing Data For the 6 examples of functors I have tried to decide all properties. There are some open cases. They are listed on the page with missing data (route `/missing`). ## Code duplication Many features for functors are very similar to the ones for categories. For now, we have a lot of copy pasted code, but this can be unified in the future. In some rare cases this has been done already (for example, the function `get_property_url` now accepts a `type` which can be `functor` or `category`). There will be a big obstacle, though: as mentioned, functor implications are more complex than category implications, since they also involve source and target assumptions. And this is actually a pattern: in the same way that a functor has two "underlying" categories, a monoidal category has one underlying category. When we add monoidal categories in the future, some implications will reference the underlying category as well. ## New Database Diagram This is the updated database diagram. All the tables on the right are new. There are many similarities, but also differences to the existing tables on the left (for categories). At some point we should also rename the old tables (`properties -> category-properties`, etc.). ![catdat-diagram](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/71c5a6f6-2747-4692-8518-d562dbd51a91) ## Documentation Of course, the documentation has been updated as well. ## Commit History The original commits have been rebased and edited *a lot*. Now you can check the individual changes by going through the commits.

body:
Adds commodity futures trading to the financial system with speculative gameplay: predict price trends via long/short positions with leverage, automatic settlement on expiry, and forced liquidation on margin calls.

## Core Implementation

**Finance System** (`js/systems/finance/FinanceSystem.js`)
- Futures contract data structure with margin mechanics (15% initial, 10% maintenance)
- Daily P&L tracking via `_processFuturesDay()` 
- Auto-settlement at expiry (7/15/30 day terms)
- Forced liquidation when equity < maintenance margin
- Fees: 0.5% closing, 2% liquidation penalty
- Position limits: 3 contracts per commodity

**Contract Lifecycle**
```javascript
// Open position with 15% margin
openFuturesPosition(state, 'food', 'long', 10, 7)
// → Daily price updates & unrealized P&L calculation
// → Auto-settles or liquidates on day 8
closeFuturesPosition(state, contractId)  // Manual close anytime
```

**API Surface**
- `getFuturesAvailableGoods()` - tradeable commodities (excludes fuel)
- `openFuturesPosition()` - create long/short contract
- `closeFuturesPosition()` - manual settlement before expiry
- `getFuturesPositions()` - active contracts with real-time P&L
- `getFuturesOverview()` - portfolio summary

## UI Integration

**Trade Station Panel** (`js/ui/TradeStationUI.js`)
- Overview: margin usage, unrealized/realized P&L with positive/negative styling
- Position cards: direction emoji (📈/📉), open/current price, days remaining, live P&L
- Quick-open buttons for each commodity
- Modal selection for direction (long/short) × duration (7/15/30 days)

**Game Manager** (`js/core/GameManager.js`)
- Event handlers `_handleOpenFutures()` and `_handleCloseFutures()`
- Modal flow for contract configuration

**Styling** (`css/panels.css`)
- `.positive` / `.negative` classes for profit/loss display

## Testing

15 test cases covering:
- Position opening (long/short), closing, fees
- Margin validation, position limits
- Auto-settlement, forced liquidation
- Multi-day price movement scenarios
- Net worth integration

All 286 tests passing.

author: copilot
body:
AnyMani lacked any written record of the effective control frequency, making it unclear how often motor commands are actually dispatched versus how fast the physics runs.

## Key finding

All environments share identical timing parameters:

```python
self.decimation = 4
self.sim.dt = 1.0 / 120.0   # 120 Hz physics
# → control frequency = 120 / 4 = 30 Hz (Δt = 33.33 ms)
```

The RL policy outputs a new action at **30 Hz**; the underlying PD actuator runs at the full **120 Hz** simulation rate, holding each action constant across 4 physics steps (Zero-Order Hold).

## Changes

- **`docs/control_frequency.md`** (new) — documents the frequency formula, decimation/ZOH mechanism, explicit `Δt = sim.dt × decimation` calculation from `recorders.py`, and a per-environment summary table with code references across all three env variants (ManagerBased joint/round-tip, Direct reorientation).
- **`README.md`** — adds the new doc to the Documentation index.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Investigate the repository's actual motor control command transmission frequency. Determine where motor commands are sent, what loop rates or timing constraints govern command dispatch, and summarize the practical control frequency for the codebase. Please inspect the relevant code paths and document the findings with file references.
> 
> The following is the prior conversation context from the user's chat exploration (may be truncated):
> 
> User: 它这里的动作控制频率是多少？
> 
> Assistant: 从仓库里的说明看，**动作/控制频率没有一个固定“控制环”写死在 API 里**，但有几个很明确的上限和示例频率：
> 
> - **示例代码里的控制循环**：`ros_example.py` 里用了 `rospy.Rate(30)`，也就是 **30 Hz**。  
> - **文档里写的查询上限**：  
>   - 只查 position：**≤ 500 Hz**  
>   - 查 position + velocity + current：**≤ 500 Hz**  
> - **C++ 注释里建议**：查询频率 **不要超过 90 samples/s**，并且 position/velocity/current 各算一次采样；所以三项一起大约相当于 **30 Hz** 更合适。
>

author: andrekurait
body:
## Problem

Workflow output parameters (e.g. `statusOutput`, `monitorResult`) are stored inline in the Workflow CR in etcd via `outputs.parameters[].valueFrom.path`. This causes two problems:

1. **etcd size limit** — Large outputs (metadata evaluation results, monitor status) can approach ~2MB. etcd has a 1MB object limit, causing workflow failures on real-world migrations with many indices.
2. **Node eviction** — If an EKS Auto Mode node is reclaimed, the pod disappears before the Argo wait container reads the output file from the container filesystem.

## Solution

Use Argo's `outputs.artifacts` instead of `outputs.parameters` for large outputs. Artifacts are uploaded to S3; only a small S3 key reference is stored in the Workflow CR. The Python CLI retrieves artifact content transparently via the Argo Server artifact API.

## Customer UX

**No changes to the user-facing CLI commands.** The artifact storage is transparent — users interact with the same commands as before:

```bash
workflow submit    # unchanged
workflow status    # artifact outputs fetched lazily from S3 via Argo API
workflow approve   # unchanged
workflow output    # large outputs stream from S3 instead of inline in etcd
```

### What changes for the user

| Aspect | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| `workflow status` output | Identical | Identical — artifact content fetched transparently |
| `workflow output` | Reads inline parameters from Workflow CR | Reads from S3 via Argo artifact API (same display) |
| Large migrations (many indices) | ❌ Fails with etcd size limit | ✅ Works — only S3 key stored in CR |
| Node eviction during output save | ❌ Output lost, step marked failed | ✅ Output persisted to S3 before pod exits |
| Workflow logs | Not archived | ✅ Archived to S3 (`archiveLogs: true`) |

### Verified on EKS with managed AOS clusters

Tested end-to-end on account `969644818851` (us-east-1):
- Source: Elasticsearch 7.10 → Target: OpenSearch 2.19
- Workflow ran through: snapshot creation → metadata evaluate → suspended at approval
- Metadata evaluation artifact successfully stored in S3 and retrieved via `workflow status`

### Bug found and fixed during testing

The Argo artifact repository Helm configuration passed an empty string for `endpoint` on EKS. Fixed by setting `endpoint` dynamically via `--set` only when LocalStack is configured; EKS uses `useSDKCreds: true` with no endpoint.

## Changes

### Layer 1: Helm — Argo Artifact Repository
- Configure `artifactRepository.s3` in Argo Helm chart values with bucket, key format, and log archiving
- `values.yaml`: secure defaults (`useStaticCredentials: false`, `insecure: false`) — no credentials in base config
- `valuesForLocalK8s.yaml`: static credentials via `argo-artifact-s3-creds` Secret, `insecure: true`
- `valuesEks.yaml`: only `useSDKCreds: true` (all other settings inherit from secure base)
- Dynamically set `bucket` and `endpoint` via `--set` in the install job
- Create `argo-artifact-s3-creds` Secret only for LocalStack environments

### Layer 2: TypeScript Builders — Artifact Output Support
- Add `OutputArtifactDef` / `OutputArtifactsRecord` types to `parameterSchemas.ts` with detailed JSDoc
- Add `addArtifactOutput()` to `ContainerBuilder` with compile-time duplicate-name blocking via `UniqueNameConstraintAtDeclaration` and `ArtifactScope` type parameter
- Add `UniqueNameConstraintAtDeclaration` to `addPathOutput()` as well
- Render `outputs.artifacts` in `argoResourceRenderer.ts`

### Layer 3: Migration Templates
- Convert `statusOutput` to artifact output in `migrationConsole.ts`
- Convert `monitorResult` to artifact output in `testMigrationWithWorkflowCli.ts`
- `overriddenPhase` stays as a parameter (tiny string used in Argo expression plumbing)

### Layer 4: Python CLI — Lazy Artifact Resolution
- `WorkflowService.create_artifact_resolver()` returns a closure with connection context baked in
- `display_workflow_tree()` accepts the resolver and invokes it lazily — only when a rendered node has an `ArtifactRef`
- `get_step_status_output()` returns `str | ArtifactRef | None` — parameters checked first, artifacts as fallback
- `WorkflowService.get_artifact_content()` fetches via Argo Server REST API
- For the ~90% of nodes without artifacts, no API call happens

### Formatting only (no semantic changes)
- `userSchemas.ts`: consistent 4-space indent, missing semicolons
- `argoSchemas.ts`: import deduplication, indent fixes

## Testing
- E2e integ tests for artifact outputs (`containerOutputs.integ.test.ts`) — submits workflows with artifact outputs to a real Argo cluster
- E2e integ test for WaitForExistingResource retry (`rendererToArgo.integ.test.ts`)
- 10 Python unit tests for artifact fetching, resolution, and display (`test_artifact_output.py`)
- All existing tests pass (112 TS unit tests, Python tests)
- End-to-end verified on EKS with managed AOS domains (ES 7.10 → OS 2.19)

body:
Change `Subgroup.normalizer` to take in a `Set G` rather than a `Subgroup G`, and deprecate `Subgroup.setNormalizer`.

This joins `Subgroup.centralizer` which is already defined on sets rather than subgroups.
Subgroups can use both of them through their `SetLike` instance.

---

Addresses this TODO on `Subgroup.setNormalizer`:
https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/34ad346d5509066e2d41dc59c6a92a917ba55661/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Defs.lean#L674
(originated in leanprover-community/mathlib3#3321)

See also https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/36760#issuecomment-4081930110

Note that `Sylow p G` has a separate `SetLike` instance (for some reason), which means there are now two defeq-but-not-syntactically-equal ways to spell "the normalizer of a Sylow p-group". To avoid modifying the statements of theorems (syntactically) this PR makes sure to always coerce them first to `Subgroup G` and then to `Set G`.

author: fukusaka
body:
## Summary

Implement IoEngine interface on the NWConnection engine (Apple Network.framework), replacing the standalone echo-loop with full Channel/ServerChannel conformance.

- **NwEngine**: `IoEngine` with suspend bind/connect, accepts `IoEngineConfig`
- **NwChannel**: Channel wrapping `nw_connection_t`, PendingWrite buffering (matching KqueueChannel), read via `keel_nw_read` (dispatch_data_t → NativeBuf copy), write/flush via `keel_nw_write`, `shutdownOutput`, `asSource()`/`asSink()` kotlinx-io bridge
- **NwServerChannel**: semaphore-based accept queue, `nw_listener_t` wrapper
- **ChannelSource/ChannelSink**: RawSource/RawSink bridge for codec layer
- **C wrappers**: `keel_nw_read`, `keel_nw_write`, `keel_nw_shutdown_output`, `keel_nw_start_conn` — replace echo-loop (`keel_nw_schedule_receive` / `keel_nw_start_connection`)
- Remove legacy echo-loop C functions

Phase (a) = synchronous I/O. suspend is for API compatibility; internal I/O blocks via dispatch semaphores. Async EventLoop (Phase (b)) deferred.

## 概要

NWConnection エンジン（Apple Network.framework）を IoEngine interface に準拠させ、スタンドアロンの echo ループを Channel/ServerChannel の完全実装に置き換える。

- **NwEngine**: `IoEngine` 実装。suspend bind/connect、`IoEngineConfig` 対応
- **NwChannel**: `nw_connection_t` ラッパー。`keel_nw_read` による受信（dispatch_data_t → NativeBuf コピー）、PendingWrite バッファリング（KqueueChannel と同パターン）、write/flush、`shutdownOutput`、`asSource()`/`asSink()` kotlinx-io ブリッジ
- **NwServerChannel**: semaphore ベースの accept キュー
- **C ラッパー**: echo ループを個別の read/write/shutdown/start に分解
- レガシー echo ループ C 関数を削除

Phase (a) = 同期 I/O。suspend は API 互換のみ、内部は dispatch semaphore でブロッキング。

### Design decisions

- **dispatch_data_t copy**: NWConnection does not provide a receive API that writes into a pre-allocated buffer. `keel_nw_read` copies via `dispatch_data_apply` + `memcpy` (~0.1–0.4 us per small packet). Accepted Phase 5 limitation; zero-copy wrapping deferred to Phase 6+ (requires NativeBuf MemoryOwner abstraction, shared with io_uring fixed buffers)
- **Semaphore-based accept**: listener new-connection handler pushes `nw_connection_t` to list, signals semaphore. `accept()` waits on semaphore, starts connection via `keel_nw_start_conn`
- **C bool workaround**: `nw_connection_receive_completion_t` has `bool` parameter incompatible with Kotlin/Native ObjC block conversion — all receive/send logic stays in C wrappers

### 設計判断

- **dispatch_data_t コピー**: NWConnection は pre-allocated buffer への受信 API を提供しない。`keel_nw_read` は `dispatch_data_apply` + `memcpy` でコピー（小パケットで ~0.1–0.4 us）。Phase 5 の意図的な制限。ゼロコピー化は Phase 6+（NativeBuf MemoryOwner 抽象、io_uring fixed buffers と統合検討）
- **Semaphore ベース accept**: listener の新接続ハンドラが `nw_connection_t` をリストに追加し semaphore を signal。`accept()` は semaphore 待機後、`keel_nw_start_conn` で接続開始
- **C bool 回避**: `nw_connection_receive_completion_t` の `bool` パラメータが Kotlin/Native ObjC ブロック変換に非対応 → receive/send ロジックを C ラッパー内に閉じ込め

## Test plan

- [x] 21 test cases
- [x] Lifecycle: 5 cases (engine/serverChannel/channel create/close)
- [x] Read/write: 6 cases (echo, EOF, flush, multi-write, index advancement)
- [x] Half-close: 2 cases (shutdownOutput FIN, read after shutdown)
- [x] Connect: 2 cases (connect, remoteAddress)
- [x] asSource/asSink: 3 cases (read, write, EOF)
- [x] Error: 3 cases (read/write/bind on closed)
- [x] `./gradlew :engine-nwconnection:macosArm64Test` — 21/21 PASS

## Remaining tasks / 残課題

- ~CHANGELOG.md `[Unreleased]` section update~ (done: 9df58c7)
- `connect()` の `localAddress` が `null` — NWConnection API で accepted connection の local endpoint 取得が困難。Phase (b) で `nw_path_copy_effective_local_endpoint` を検討
- macosX64 テスト未実施（macosArm64 のみ確認）

在 WPF 动画中，设置动画目标属性的关键在于理解目标元素的属性结构。以下是简单明了的规则：
一、直接属性（如 Opacity、Width）
直接在 Storyboard.TargetProperty 中写属性名即可：
`<DoubleAnimation Storyboard.TargetProperty="Opacity" From="0" To="1" ... />
`或显式指定类型：
`<DoubleAnimation Storyboard.TargetProperty="(UIElement.Opacity)" ... />`
二、单一变换（如 TranslateTransform）
如果元素的 RenderTransform 只包含一种变换（例如 TranslateTransform），路径为：
`(UIElement.RenderTransform).(TranslateTransform.X)`
示例：
`<DoubleAnimation Storyboard.TargetProperty="(UIElement.RenderTransform).(TranslateTransform.X)" From="400" To="0"/>`
三、变换组（TransformGroup）
如果 RenderTransform 是 TransformGroup（包含多个子变换），需要通过 Children 索引定位具体子项：
```
RenderTransform.Children[0].ScaleX   <!-- 第一个子变换的 ScaleX -->
RenderTransform.Children[1].Angle    <!-- 第二个子变换的 Angle -->
```
示例：
`<DoubleAnimation Storyboard.TargetProperty="RenderTransform.Children[0].ScaleX" From="1" To="1.1"/>`


关键检查点

- 确保 RenderTransform 已设置：在样式或本地必须显式定义 RenderTransform，否则属性不存在，动画无效。
- 索引与顺序一致：Children 索引必须与 XAML 中定义的子变换顺序完全一致（0 起始）。
- 类型匹配：动画目标属性必须是 double 类型，且变换类有对应属性（如 ScaleX、Angle、X 等）。

在 WPF 动画中，设置动画目标属性需要根据属性的实际结构来决定路径写法：

1. 如果要动画的元素直接属性（如 Opacity、Width），路径直接写属性名即可，例如 Opacity。
2. 如果元素的 RenderTransform 只包含一种变换（如 TranslateTransform），路径需要写成 (UIElement.RenderTransform).(TranslateTransform.X) 这样的格式，先取 RenderTransform 再转换为具体变换类型后访问其属性。
3. 如果 RenderTransform 是一个 TransformGroup 包含多个子变换，则必须通过 Children 索引来定位，例如 RenderTransform.Children[0].ScaleX 表示第一个子变换（通常是 ScaleTransform）的 ScaleX 属性。

关键检查点包括：确保 RenderTransform 已在样式或本地显式设置，Children 索引必须与 XAML 中定义的子变换顺序一致，动画目标属性必须是 double 类型且变换类有对应属性。

author: leecheneler
body:
## Summary

Adds the foundational provider client for connecting to any OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint (Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, etc.) with streaming support.

## GitHub Issue

Closes #36

## What Changed

Two new modules in `src/provider/`:

- **SSE parser** — async generator that reads a `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>`, buffers partial lines across chunks, yields `data:` payloads, and terminates on `[DONE]`. Handles both `\n` and `\r\n` line endings.
- **Provider client** — `streamChatCompletion()` function that POSTs to `{baseUrl}/v1/chat/completions` with `stream: true` and yields content strings via async generator. Wraps connection failures and HTTP errors with clear messages. Accepts an `AbortSignal` for cancellation (used later for Escape-to-interrupt).

Also added `vitest/globals` to `tsconfig.json` types to fix VS Code type resolution for test files.

16 new tests covering SSE parsing edge cases (chunked data, `[DONE]` sentinel, `\r\n`, trailing buffers) and client behaviour (request shape, error handling, abort signals, role-only deltas).

author: samggreenberg
body:
## Summary
Fixes a bug where running the `/api/find-label` endpoint would overwrite a trainable model's saved training labels with scoring results from a different dataset. The fix introduces a "find mode" flag that prevents label synchronization when a model is used for scoring.

## Key Changes
- **Added find mode tracking** (`_find_mode` flag in `registry.py`):
  - New `is_find_mode()` and `set_find_mode()` functions to manage find mode state
  - Find mode is automatically cleared when a new model is loaded via `set_loaded_id()`
  - Find mode is reset during test cleanup

- **Updated label synchronization logic** (`trainable_models.py`):
  - `sync_labels_to_loaded_model()` now skips synchronization when the model is in find mode
  - Prevents scoring results from overwriting the model's original training labels

- **Set find mode after scoring** (`detectors_scoring.py`):
  - `/api/find-label` endpoint now sets find mode to `True` after scoring completes
  - Ensures subsequent votes won't sync the scoring labels back to the model

- **Added comprehensive test** (`test_detectors.py`):
  - `test_find_label_does_not_overwrite_training_labels()` reproduces the original bug scenario
  - Verifies that training labels persist after find-label scoring on a different dataset
  - `test_find_mode_cleared_on_model_load()` ensures find mode is cleared when loading a new model

## Implementation Details
The solution uses a simple state flag rather than complex label tracking, making it easy to understand and maintain. Find mode is automatically managed—it's set when scoring occurs and cleared when a new model is loaded, so users don't need to manually manage this state.

This pull request is to address a problem where deepcopying a `MaskedColumn` resulted in the loss of the `info._format_funcs` attribute. The higher level problem noted in #19408 is that a deepcopied `Table` with a masked column would no longer print.

AI figured out the problem, wrote the initial solution 6321c22 and the test. @taldcroft authored subsequent commits.

<!-- If the pull request closes any open issues you can add this.
If you replace <Issue Number> with a number, GitHub will automatically link it.
If this pull request is unrelated to any issues, please remove
the following line. -->
Fixes #19408

#### AI-generated explanation of the problem

I could not figure this out, but Copilot got me there in a few minutes.

##### What is happening

`Column` and `MaskedColumn` both rely on Astropy’s `info` descriptor machinery, where a **bound** info object initializes `_format_funcs = {}` for print-format caching.

For `Column`, both `copy.copy()` and `copy.deepcopy()` end up with a correctly bound `info`, so `_format_funcs` is present.

For `MaskedColumn`, `copy.copy()` behaves as expected, but `copy.deepcopy()` can leave an `info` object that is missing `_format_funcs`, even though a bound `info` appears to have been created earlier in the call path.

##### Why `MaskedColumn` is different

`MaskedColumn` inherits from `numpy.ma.MaskedArray`, so deepcopy behavior goes through `MaskedArray.__deepcopy__`.

NumPy’s `MaskedArray.__deepcopy__` effectively:

1. Creates a copied masked-array instance.
2. Iterates through `self.__dict__` and deep-copies each entry directly into `copied.__dict__`.

That second step is the key. If `info` is already materialized in `self.__dict__`, NumPy deep-copies that raw `info` object directly, bypassing Astropy’s descriptor rebinding path.

##### Why `_format_funcs` disappears

Astropy’s `DataInfo`/`BaseColumnInfo` uses slots and custom state handling. The deep-copied `info` object preserves `_attrs` (for example, `serialize_method`), but `_format_funcs` is a bound-time cache and not part of the normal serialized attribute state.

So after direct `__dict__` deepcopy, the copied `info` can keep metadata in `_attrs` while lacking bound-only cache state like `_format_funcs`.

In short:

- metadata survives (`_attrs`)
- bound cache state does not (`_format_funcs`)

##### Why this is tied to `MaskedArray.__deepcopy__`

Yes, this behavior is directly related to NumPy masked-array deepcopy internals.

The normal Astropy descriptor path that creates/rebinds `info` (and initializes bound state) is bypassed when NumPy directly copies `info` out of `__dict__`. That is why the issue appears in `MaskedColumn` deepcopy but not in plain `Column` deepcopy.

##### Why the debug print still appears

(I had put in a debug print statement showing that the init was being called and creating the `_format_funcs` attribute, but then after the object was fully created it was gone. That is where I got stuck.)

The debug print in `BaseColumnInfo.__init__(bound=True)` shows that a bound `info` object is created at some point.

However, during `MaskedColumn` deepcopy, a later direct `__dict__` deep-copy step can overwrite that freshly bound `info` with a raw deep-copied `info` object that lacks `_format_funcs`.

So the print is accurate, but it does not reflect the final object state after all deepcopy steps complete.

author: copilot
body:
Claude Code CLI validates `agents` and `skills` in plugin.json as `array<string>` per its manifest schema. Our plugins declared these as directory path strings (e.g. `"agents": "./agents/"`, `"skills": "./skills/"`), causing install failures:

> Error: Failed to install: Plugin has an invalid manifest file. Validation errors: agents: Invalid input

Per the [Copilot CLI plugin reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-plugin-reference), both `agents` and `skills` field types are `string | string[]` with values being "Path(s) to directories". The simplified directory-path array form `["./agents/"]` / `["./skills/"]` satisfies both Claude Code CLI (requires array) and Copilot CLI (accepts both).

### Changes

- **Convert `"agents"` to a directory-path array** in 3 plugin.json files (`dotnet-diag`, `dotnet-msbuild`, `dotnet-template-engine`) — using `["./agents/"]`
- **Convert `"skills"` to a directory-path array** in all 10 plugin.json files — using `["./skills/"]`
- **Consolidate `PluginInfo` model** — replaced the dual `SkillsPath` (string) / `SkillPaths` (array) and `AgentsPath` (string) / `AgentPaths` (array) fields with single `SkillPaths` and `AgentPaths` fields (`IReadOnlyList<string>`). The parser normalizes legacy string values into single-element arrays, so all downstream code uses one field with no fallback branching.
- **Update `ParsePluginJson`** to read both `skills` and `agents` as string arrays first (preferred, Claude Code schema) and normalize plain strings into single-element arrays
- **Update `ValidatePlugin`** to validate array entries as either directories or files for both fields (safety checks + existence)
- **Update `DiscoverSkillsInPlugin` and `DiscoverAgentsInPlugin`** to handle array entries as directories (discovering all files within) or individual files
- **Update `AgentRunner` and `CheckCommand`** to resolve skill directories from the array fields
- **Remove accidentally committed `.nuget/nuget.exe` binary**

```diff
-"skills": "./skills/"
+"skills": ["./skills/"]
```

```diff
-"agents": "./agents/"
+"agents": ["./agents/"]
```

body:
The platform runs entirely on mock data from `src/lib/data.ts` with no real database. This PR wires in Prisma ORM v5 against PostgreSQL as the data layer foundation, without replacing mock-data consumers yet.

## Schema (`prisma/schema.prisma`)
Six core models with proper relations and cascade deletes:
- `User` — credentials, role enum (`admin` / `instructor` / `member`), optional avatar/bio
- `Course` → `Module` → `Lesson` — fully nested, `tags String[]`, `level` enum
- `Subscription` — one-to-one with `User`, plan/status enums, auto-renew flag
- `Payment` — many-to-one with `User`, method + status enum

## Infrastructure
- **`src/lib/prisma.ts`** — `PrismaClient` singleton guarded via `globalThis` (prevents duplicate instances under Next.js hot-reload)

## Summary

This change aligns the web UI with the API authorization rules for skills management.

Until now, any authenticated user could see admin-only catalog actions in the skills screen, even though the backend correctly restricted them to `ADMIN`. That created a misleading and unprofessional UX for a portfolio project.

## Changes

- added `role` to the frontend auth user model

- hid edit and activate/deactivate catalog actions for non-admin users
- updated frontend tests to cover admin vs non-admin rendering

## Why

This does not fix a backend security issue, because the API already enforced permissions correctly. It fixes a frontend authorization inconsistency that made the product feel incomplete and incorrectly exposed admin capabilities in the UI.

author: michaelkatsoulis
body:
This PR addresses the following two problems:

When batching was enabled with CloudWatch output, multiple generated records were concatenated into a single CloudWatch log event message, causing downstream parsers to fail because they received more data than expected in one event. 
As an example VPC Flow logs stored in CloudWatch Log group consisted of 28 fields instead of 14 as two flow logs were concatenated into one.

cloudtrail.go fix: 
Changed `GetAndReset()` to emit all accumulated CloudTrail records as NDJSON (one JSON object per line) instead of only emitting `c.current[0]` and silently discarding the rest of the batch.

author: morapelker
body:
## Summary

- **Persistent PR attachment model**: Worktrees can now have a GitHub PR persistently attached via new `github_pr_number` and `github_pr_url` database columns (schema v10 migration). PRs survive app restarts and are stored in SQLite rather than ephemeral in-memory state.
- **PR picker popover**: Replaces the old inline PR state badge with a Popover-based PR picker. Clicking the PR badge opens a dropdown listing all open PRs (sorted with branch-matching PR first), allowing users to switch or detach the attached PR.
- **Live PR state queries**: New `git:getPRState` IPC channel uses `gh pr view` to fetch real-time PR state (open/merged/closed) and title, displayed in the PR badge and picker header.
- **Full-stack IPC plumbing**: New `db:worktree:attachPR` and `db:worktree:detachPR` IPC handlers with corresponding preload bridge methods (`window.db.worktree.attachPR/detachPR`) and type declarations.
- **Git store refactor**: Replaced the old `prInfo` map (with `state: 'none' | 'creating' | 'created' | 'merged'`) with two separate maps — `prCreation` (transient creation-in-progress tracking) and `attachedPR` (persistent PR attachment synced to DB). Added `attachPR()`, `detachPR()`, and `loadAttachedPR()` store actions.
- **PR detection hook update**: `usePRDetection` now calls `attachPR()` on the store (which persists to DB) when a PR URL is detected in session output, instead of the old `setPrState()`.
- **Header UI overhaul**: The PR button area now has three distinct states — "Create PR" button (no PR attached), spinner (PR being created), and PR badge with popover (PR attached). Merge and Archive buttons now derive visibility from live PR state rather than in-memory state.
- **New Popover component**: Added `src/renderer/src/components/ui/popover.tsx` (Radix-based shadcn popover primitive).
- **Code formatting**: Prettier reformatting across ~30 files (import grouping, JSX formatting, SVG attribute splitting, line-length compliance).

## Test plan

- [ ] Create a new worktree and verify the PR button shows "PR" (no attachment)
- [ ] Click PR to create one via AI session — verify spinner shows during creation
- [ ] After PR is created and detected, verify the PR badge shows `PR #N`
- [ ] Click the PR badge — verify the popover lists open PRs with the attached one highlighted
- [ ] Select a different PR from the picker — verify the badge updates
- [ ] Click "Detach PR" — verify badge disappears and "Create PR" button returns
- [ ] Restart the app — verify the attached PR persists across restarts
- [ ] Verify merged PRs show "· merged" suffix and the Archive button appears
- [ ] Verify closed PRs show "· closed" and the Merge button is hidden

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Introduces a schema migration and new IPC-backed state for persisting PR metadata on worktrees, plus UI logic that changes merge/archive behavior based on live `gh` queries. Risk is mainly around migration correctness and PR lifecycle edge cases (attach/detach/creation) across restarts.
> 
> **Overview**
> Worktrees can now persist an *attached GitHub PR* via new `worktrees.github_pr_number`/`worktrees.github_pr_url` columns (schema v10) with new DB methods and IPC endpoints (`db:worktree:attachPR`/`detachPR`) and preload wiring.
> 
> The PR lifecycle state in the renderer is refactored: transient `prCreation` tracks an in-progress PR-creation session, while `attachedPR` is persisted/rehydrated from the DB; `usePRDetection` now attaches PRs by persisting the detected PR URL instead of updating an in-memory PR state.
> 
> Header PR UI is overhauled to show a create button, a creating spinner, or an attached PR badge with a popover picker (list/switch/detach), and merge/archive button visibility now keys off a new `git:getPRState` IPC call that queries `gh pr view` for live PR state/title. Most other changes are formatting-only.

This is a sync of all of Juthisarker's iterations on the [ETL](https://exercism.org/tracks/go/exercises/etl) exercise on [Exercism's](https://exercism.org) [Go Track](https://exercism.org/tracks/go).

It has been automatically generated at the request of Juthisarker using Exercism's GitHub Solution Syncer tool.

---

_[Exercism](https://exercism.org) is a leading non-profit coding education platform. We help people from all over the world learn and practice over 75 different programming languages for free! 🚀_

## Problem

The `05-entraid-3lo-gateway` tutorial fails during `cdk deploy` with two conflicting validation errors:

1. **CDK synth** rejects the OpenAPI spec because it contains a top-level `security` array — the `@aws-cdk/aws-bedrock-agentcore-alpha` construct validates that authentication must be configured via the Gateway's outbound authorization config instead.

2. **CloudFormation** (the service-side `AWS::BedrockAgentCore::GatewayTarget` resource handler) rejects the spec if `components.securitySchemes` is missing, returning: `attribute components.securitySchemes.entraId.type is missing`.

## Fix

- Remove the top-level `security` array and per-operation `security` entries from `weather-api.json` (satisfies CDK construct validation)
- Keep `components.securitySchemes` intact (satisfies CloudFormation service-side validation)
- Bump CDK dependencies to latest versions (`aws-cdk-lib` 2.243.0, `@aws-cdk/aws-bedrock-agentcore-alpha` 2.243.0-alpha.0)

## Testing

Verified `cdk synth` passes cleanly with the updated spec on the latest CDK construct version.

The main enhancements include better documentation, clearer troubleshooting steps, and improved automation for detecting and providing M365 credentials.

**Key improvements are grouped below:**

**Automation & Credential Handling:**
- Enhanced the `hooks/postprovision.ps1` script to support additional environment variables for M365 connectivity and credentials (e.g., `dagaConnectM365`, `dagaM365UserPrincipalName`), and added auto-detection of the M365 UPN from the Azure CLI login if not explicitly set.
