author: rishabhjava
body:
## Summary

- Adds `whop/charge` as a third payment method alongside `tempo` and `stripe`
- Uses Whop's existing public API — **no Whop backend changes required**
- Server creates a checkout configuration, client completes payment via Whop Checkout, server verifies via `payments.retrieve()`
- Includes client SDK, server SDK, CLI plugin, proxy service, working example, and 20 passing tests

## How it works

```
Agent → GET /resource → 402 (challenge with Whop checkout URL)
Agent → opens checkout, user pays → gets payment ID
Agent → retries with payment ID as credential
Server → verifies via Whop API → 200 + receipt
```

### Server
```ts
import { Mppx, whop } from 'mppx/server'

const mppx = Mppx.create({
  methods: [whop({ apiKey: process.env.WHOP_API_KEY!, companyId: 'biz_xxx' })],
})
```

### Client
```ts
import { Mppx, whop } from 'mppx/client'

const mppx = Mppx.create({
  methods: [whop({ completeCheckout: async ({ purchaseUrl }) => { ... } })],
})
```

### Composable with existing methods
```ts
const mppx = Mppx.create({
  methods: [
    tempo.charge({ currency: USDC, recipient: '0x...' }),
    whop({ apiKey: WHOP_KEY, companyId: 'biz_xxx' }),
  ],
})
```

## Files

| Path | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `src/whop/Methods.ts` | Method definition (name: `whop`, intent: `charge`) |
| `src/whop/client/Charge.ts` | Client credential creation via `completeCheckout` callback |
| `src/whop/server/Charge.ts` | Server verification via Whop `payments.retrieve()` + `createCheckout` utility |
| `src/whop/internal/types.ts` | Duck-typed `WhopClient` interface |
| `src/cli/plugins/whop.ts` | CLI plugin (opens browser, prompts for payment ID) |
| `src/proxy/services/whop.ts` | Whop proxy service definition |
| `examples/whop/` | Working Vite example ($1 fortune cookie) |
| `src/whop/**/*.test.ts` | 20 tests (schema, client, server, receipts) |

## Test plan

- [x] `src/whop/Methods.test.ts` — schema validation (9 tests)
- [x] `src/whop/client/Charge.test.ts` — client credential creation (5 tests)
- [x] `src/whop/server/Charge.test.ts` — server verification, error handling, receipts (6 tests)
- [x] Type-check passes (`pnpm check:types`)
- [x] Example tested locally against live Whop API with real payments

## Summary

### FDE-81 — Custom appBar slot
- \`ChatScreen\` accepts an optional \`appBar: (@Composable () -> Unit)?\` parameter
- When provided it replaces the built-in \`ChatAppBar\`; when null the default renders unchanged

### FDE-80 — Shop / cart callbacks wired to ChatAppBar
- \`ChatScreen\` accepts \`onShopPressed\` and \`onCartPressed\` lambdas, matching Flutter SDK's \`Chat(onShopPressed:, onCartPressed:)\` params
- Correctly placed in \`ChatAppBar\` as \`IconButton\` actions — aligns with Flutter reference implementation
- \`ChatAppBar\` renders \`theme.chatIconImage\` as a circular avatar when set

### API base URL hidden from public API
- \`apiBaseUrl\` removed from \`YaloChatConfig\` (consumer-facing)
- Injected at build time via \`local.properties\` / \`YALO_API_BASE_URL\` env var, mirroring Flutter's \`--dart-define\` pattern
- Production consumers never configure the URL; CI injects it via secret

### Endpoint switch: /webchat/ → /inapp/
- \`sendTextMessage\` moved from \`POST /webchat/inbound_messages\` → \`POST /inapp/inbound_messages\`
- \`fetchMessages\` moved from \`GET /webchat/messages\` → \`GET /inapp/messages\`
- Aligns the Android SDK with the inapp channel contract (Flutter/web use /webchat/ because they are webchat integrations; Android is an inapp SDK)

### Proto codegen — replace hand-written DTOs with committed proto/kotlin/
- Deletes hand-written \`YaloTextMessageRequest\` / \`YaloTextMessage\`; replaced by proto-generated Kotlin DSL + thin \`SdkMessageBody\` JSON adapter for Ktor (protobuf-kotlin-lite has no JsonFormat)
- \`YaloMessageRepositoryRemote\` builds outgoing messages with \`sdkMessage { textMessageRequest { } }\` DSL
- \`proto/kotlin/\` is added as a Gradle source directory (\`java.srcDir\`), consumed directly at compile time — same pattern as flutter-sdk/web-sdk consuming \`proto/dart/\` and \`proto/typescript/\` via symlinks; source is always readable in the repo
- \`proto_kotlin\` Makefile target added for regenerating \`proto/kotlin/\` alongside \`proto_dart\`, \`proto_ts\`, \`proto_go\`
- \`com/google/protobuf/Generated.kt\` stub added: Makefile-generated files use \`@file:com.google.protobuf.Generated\` which only exists in protobuf-java (non-lite); \`SOURCE\` retention means it is erased from .class files and never shipped in the .aar

### Tests
- \`StagingIntegrationTest\`: exercises auth + \`GET /inapp/messages\` against staging2 end-to-end; gated behind \`STAGING_INTEGRATION=1\`; credentials read from env vars
- \`YaloMessageRepositoryRemoteTest\`: updated JSON fixtures to proto3 wire format; role strings use \`MESSAGE_ROLE_AGENT\` / \`MESSAGE_ROLE_USER\` encoding; added role-defaulting test

author: copilot
body:
`ishita-git16.github.io/vibe-coding/` was rendering blank because two workflows were racing to deploy to GitHub Pages — and the Jekyll workflow was winning by deploying **unbuilt source files**.

## Root cause

`jekyll-gh-pages.yml` served the raw source `index.html` which contains:
```html
<script type="module" src="/src/main.jsx"></script>
```
That path doesn't exist on GitHub Pages (no bundler ran), so React never mounted and the page stayed blank.

## Fix

- **Deleted** `.github/workflows/jekyll-gh-pages.yml` — this repo is a Vite/React SPA, not a Jekyll site; the workflow was added erroneously
- `deploy.yml` remains as the sole deployment pipeline: it runs `npm run build`, uploads `dist/`, and deploys it
- `vite.config.js` already has `base: '/vibe-coding/'` so all built asset references resolve correctly under the Pages subpath

**🕸️ Tangle:** 
The integration test `workspace_smoke.rs` was placed inside the `orpheus-pattern` leaf crate. Because this test relies on higher-level crates (`orpheus-dsp` and `orpheus-lang`), it forced `orpheus-pattern` to include them in its `dev-dependencies`. This created a cyclic dependency loop in the workspace test graph (`orpheus-lang` -> `orpheus-dsp` -> `orpheus-pattern` -> `orpheus-lang` [dev]).

**📏 Blueprint:** 
Moved the `workspace_smoke.rs` integration test to the root workspace `tests/` directory. This naturally refactors the workspace to test integration at the top level, allowing the `orpheus-pattern` crate to drop the extraneous `dev-dependencies` and restoring a strictly acyclic dependency graph.

**🧱 Stability:** 
Reduced coupling and eliminated the cyclic dev-dependency loop. Compiles and tests without side-effects since `workspace_smoke.rs` already accessed the crates via their external public APIs.

**🔬 Verification:** 
Ran `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy`, and `cargo tree -d` successfully to confirm the cyclic dependency is gone and code correctly works.

author: japacx
body:
## Summary
The `openspec-plan` agent previously only declared `edit` permissions, leaving
all other tools (read, bash, glob, grep, etc.) as implicit — relying on
OpenCode's global defaults. 

This made the agent's actual capabilities opaque and created a risk of unintended access.

This PR replaces the minimal permission block with a fully explicit declaration
covering every OpenCode permission key relevant to the agent.

## Changes
**`src/config.ts`** — `openSpecAgent.permission`
### read
- Allow all file reads
- Explicitly deny `.env` files (a spec agent has no need for secrets)
### edit
- Base rule: `"*": "deny"` — nothing is editable by default
- Explicit `allow` only for spec targets: `project.md`, `AGENTS.md`,
  `openspec/**`, `specs/**`
### bash
- Base rule: `"*": "deny"` — no arbitrary shell execution
- Allow read-only filesystem commands: `grep`, `ls`, `cat`, `find`,
  `echo`, `pwd`, `which`, `env`, `printenv`
- Allow git read-only: `git status*`, `git log*`, `git diff*`, `git show*`
  (useful for repo context without risk of mutations)
### All other tools
Explicitly declared as `allow` or `ask` instead of relying on defaults:
- `glob`, `grep`, `list`, `lsp` — allow (read-only exploration)
- `todoread`, `todowrite` — allow (internal task tracking)
- `webfetch`, `websearch`, `codesearch` — allow (doc/reference lookup)
- `task`, `skill`, `question` — allow (subagents and user interaction)
- `doom_loop`, `external_directory` — ask (safety guards, unchanged)
## Why last-match-wins matters here
OpenCode evaluates granular permission rules in order, with the **last matching
rule winning**. For `edit` and `bash`, the catch-all `"*": "deny"` is placed
first so that the specific `allow` rules after it correctly override it.
## No functional change for spec files
The set of files the agent can edit is identical to before. This PR only makes
the full permission surface explicit and adds a deny baseline for everything
outside that set.

author: felixtjdietrich
body:
## Description

Implements the `JobTypeHandler` methods (`prepareInputFiles`, `buildPrompt`) for practice-aware PR review in `PullRequestReviewHandler`. The handler now assembles structured prompts from workspace practice definitions and PR context, with an output contract aligned to `PracticeDetectionResultParser`.

Closes #853

### What changed (5 files, +595/-55)

**`PullRequestReviewHandler.java`** (+248/-55) — Core implementation:
- `prepareInputFiles()`: Now writes `.context/practices.json` containing active practice definitions (slug, name, category, description, detectionPrompt) for the workspace. Validates workspace is assigned and at least 1 active practice exists.
- `buildPrompt()`: Completely rewritten from a generic code review prompt to a practice-aware prompt using `StringBuilder`. Includes:
  - Practice definitions as structured markdown headings (prefers `detectionPrompt`, falls back to `description`)
  - Verdict semantics (POSITIVE/NEGATIVE/NOT_APPLICABLE/NEEDS_REVIEW) with clear definitions
  - Severity/verdict orthogonality explained with concrete examples to prevent LLM confusion
  - JSON output contract matching `PracticeDetectionResultParser.ValidatedFinding` schema exactly — all enum values (Verdict, Severity, CaMethod), field constraints, and confidence semantics
  - No markdown fences in JSON examples (prevents agents from wrapping output in fences, which breaks parsing)
- Added `buildPracticeDefinitions()` private helper for JSON serialization of Practice entities
- Both lifecycle methods independently query `PracticeRepository` — documented trade-off since the handler is a singleton bean and the SPI doesn't support passing data between calls (mirrors `PracticeDetectionDeliveryService` pattern)

**`JobTypeHandlerConfiguration.java`** (+3) — Injects `PracticeRepository` into the handler bean.

**`JobTypeHandler.java`** (+1) — Added `@throws JobPreparationException` Javadoc to `buildPrompt()`.

**`PullRequestReviewHandlerTest.java`** (+393) — 54 unit tests across 5 nested classes:
- Practice JSON serialization (null fields omitted, categories conditional, detectionPrompt presence)
- Practice-aware prompt structure (headings, categories, detection prompt vs description fallback, verdict meanings, severity/verdict disambiguation examples)
- Output contract alignment: programmatically iterates all `Verdict`, `Severity`, `CaMethod` enum values to verify they appear in the prompt
- Edge cases: null workspace, empty practices, null instructions, percent characters in metadata
- Delivery pipeline: `ArgumentCaptor` verification of parsed findings, valid+invalid filtering, exception propagation

**`JobTypeHandlerRegistryTest.java`** (+5) — Updated constructor call for new `PracticeRepository` parameter.

### Design decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|
| Double practice query (prepareInputFiles + buildPrompt) | Handler is a singleton bean; SPI has no shared-state mechanism. Cheap indexed query. Same pattern as `PracticeDetectionDeliveryService`. |
| StringBuilder over String.formatted() | Metadata fields may contain `%` characters that would be misinterpreted as format specifiers. |
| Prompt limits (2K/1K) stricter than parser limits (10K/5K) | Keeps agent output concise while parser provides tolerance for overruns. |
| No markdown fences in JSON schema | LLMs imitate example formatting — fences cause agents to wrap output in fences, breaking JSON parsing. |
| Fail-fast on empty practices | A job with no active practices cannot produce meaningful findings; surface the error early. |

### Prompt ↔ Parser contract alignment (verified)

| Prompt Field | Parser Handling | Aligned? |
|---|---|---|
| `practiceSlug` (required) | `textField` + blank check + slug normalization (lowercase, `_` → `-`) | Yes |
| `title` (required, max 255) | `textField` + blank check + truncation at 255 | Yes |
| `verdict` (POSITIVE/NEGATIVE/NOT_APPLICABLE/NEEDS_REVIEW) | `parseEnum(Verdict.class)` | Yes |
| `severity` (CRITICAL/MAJOR/MINOR/INFO) | `parseEnum(Severity.class)` | Yes |
| `confidence` (float 0.0-1.0) | `parseConfidence()` with auto percentage-to-decimal conversion | Yes |
| `evidence` (optional JSON) | Size-capped at 64KB, opaque JsonNode | Yes |
| `reasoning` (optional, "under 2K chars") | `optionalTextField`, truncated at 10K | Yes |
| `guidance` (optional, "under 1K chars") | `optionalTextField`, truncated at 5K | Yes |
| `guidanceMethod` (optional enum) | Best-effort `CaMethod` parse, null on failure | Yes |

### Database schema alignment (verified via psql)

- `practice` table: slug(NOT NULL), name(NOT NULL), description(NOT NULL TEXT), detection_prompt(nullable TEXT), is_active(NOT NULL) — all null-checks in handler match schema constraints
- `practice_finding` table: CHECK constraints for verdict, severity, guidance_method, confidence match prompt enum values exactly
- `idx_practice_workspace_active` index covers `findByWorkspaceIdAndActiveTrue` query

## How to test

1. **Unit tests** (54 tests, all passing):
   ```bash
   cd server/application-server
   mvn test -Dgroups=unit -Dtest="PullRequestReviewHandlerTest,JobTypeHandlerRegistryTest" -DskipTests=false -Dmaven.test.skip=false
   ```

2. **Manual verification** — The handler is invoked by `AgentJobExecutor` during agent job execution. To test end-to-end:
   - Create a workspace with active practices in the database
   - Trigger a `PULL_REQUEST_REVIEW` job via the agent pipeline
   - Verify `.context/practices.json` is written to the container volume
   - Verify the prompt contains practice headings and output contract

3. **Key test scenarios covered**:
   - Practice definitions serialized correctly (with/without category, with/without detectionPrompt)
   - Prompt includes all enum values from Verdict, Severity, CaMethod
   - Fail-fast when workspace is null or no active practices exist
   - Delivery pipeline correctly filters valid/invalid findings via ArgumentCaptor
   - Diff truncation with UTF-8 boundary safety

author: micbase
body:
exec.inspect().Pid returns the host-namespace PID, which doesn't exist inside the container's PID namespace. Running `kill` inside the container with that PID always silently failed, leaving the old server running and causing "port in use" errors on restart.

Fix: wrap the start command to write the shell's own `$$` (container PID) to a temp file before exec-ing the real command, then read it back when killing. Also cleans up the pid file on stop/clear.

author: aanderse
body:
i think `nixos-facter` could be _very_ useful for other nix based oses, like [finix](https://github.com/finix-community/finix)

i built `nixos-facter` with this code using [libudev-zero](https://github.com/illiliti/libudev-zero) and it produces useful `json` on my non-systemd based system

built via `pkgs.nixos-facter.override { systemdMinimal = pkgs.libudev-zero; }`

the basic idea is that since `libudev-zero` can provide the same information as `udev` we can just make the `udev` version check optional if `udevadm` isn't available... ie. we're on a system that isn't `systemd` based


... let me know what you think :eyes:

author: nipunayf
body:
## Purpose

Simplify the compiler-engine snapshot API so callers work with a single
materialized stable snapshot type instead of raw compiler artifacts and
duplicate snapshot wrappers.

## Approach

Promoted `StableSnapshot` to the concrete final snapshot type, folded the
materialized fields and path-based accessors into it, and reduced
`CompilationService` to a single `stableSnapshot()` method. Updated the
service implementation, facade callers, and factory wiring to use the new
shape, then removed the redundant snapshot classes.

## What Was Fixed / Changed

- Replaced the three-method compilation service contract with
  `stableSnapshot(Path, CancelChecker)`.
- Added blocking stable-snapshot lookup in `CompilationServiceImpl` when no
  stable snapshot is immediately available.
- Updated facade query paths to read syntax trees, semantic models, and
  compilations from the stable snapshot.
- Consolidated snapshot construction in the workspace factory.
- Removed the obsolete `MaterializedStableSnapshot` and `ProjectSnapshot`
  types.
- Updated tests and contract checks to match the new API.

## Affected Components

- `langserver-core/src/main/java/org/ballerinalang/langserver/workspace/compilerengine`
- `langserver-core/src/main/java/org/ballerinalang/langserver/workspace/lspgateway`
- `langserver-core/src/main/java/org/ballerinalang/langserver/workspace`
- `langserver-core/src/test/java/org/ballerinalang/langserver/workspace`

## How Has This Been Tested

Ran `langserver-core` compile and focused test suites covering the new
snapshot contract, facade delegation, compiler-engine value objects, and the
affected acceptance/regression tests. Targeted runs passed after the refactor.

## Remarks & Notes

Some broader test runs emitted existing Docker-daemon warnings from the test
environment, but the relevant `langserver-core` test targets passed. No
intentional behavior changes were made outside the snapshot API refactor.

body:
## Summary

- Replaces the CSS-only `css-policy-touch-target` rule with `jsx-layout-policy-touch-target` — a cross-file Layout graph rule that resolves cascade values including Tailwind utilities and component-scoped CSS, catching undersized interactive elements the old rule missed (e.g. `<button class="p-0">` wrapping an `<Avatar size="sm">`)

- Adds `noReservedBlockSize` / `noReservedInlineSize` diagnostics for interactive elements with no declared height/width using the existing `ReservedSpaceFact` infrastructure — content-sized elements like the avatar button case are now flagged instead of silently skipped

- Fixes `diagCache` poisoning bug where `publishFileDiagnostics` (line 188) and `republishMergedDiagnostics` (line 254) stored merged single+cross-file diagnostics back into `diagCache`, violating the single-file-only invariant documented at `runDiagnostics` lines 36-38 — this caused double-counted cross-file diagnostics in the pull handler and stale diagnostics persisting after AI agent edits

- Adds optional `Logger` parameter to `resolveTailwindValidator` with granular logging at each failure point (no entry file, `@tailwindcss/node` unresolvable, missing export, design system load failure) — threads the logger through all three async callers (`lifecycle.ts`, `lint.ts`, `daemon.ts`) for diagnosing Tailwind detection failures in monorepo setups

- Adds `[PULL-DIAG]` info-level logging to the pull diagnostic handler showing `warningsAsErrors` flag state, single-file/cross-file counts, fileIndex presence, and LSP severity breakdown — guarded with `isLevelEnabled` checks

- Updates `packages/vscode/package.json` rule reference from `css-policy-touch-target` to `jsx-layout-policy-touch-target`

- Deletes old CSS rule `css-policy-touch-target.ts` and its 11 CSS-only tests, adds 24 cross-file tests covering height/width/padding violations, element detection, Tailwind utilities, visually hidden elements, rem conversion, component host resolution, and all `noReservedSize` edge cases

- Bumps all four packages to `0.2.72`

body:
Adds way more fuel types plus a .java-version file so IntelliJ automatically picks Java 25 when cloning the Project.

## What changed

~55 new fluid entries across all four fuel categories covering HBM's oil refining chain, gas processing, and steam tiers. Re-sorted the whole file by energy density (low to high) and corrected a couple existing values (diesel 39.1 to 38.6 MJ/L, gasoline 25.8 to 32.2 MJ/L because old values were off vs real-world LHV).

- dieselFuels (5 -> 30): crude oils, cracked/desulfurized/hot variants, bio-oils, bitumen, heating oil, lubricant, diesel reform chain
- gasolineFuels (13 -> 27): ethanol, naphtha chain, petroil, gasoline + leaded, light oil variants, reformed kerosene, aromatics, reformate, unsaturateds
- gasFuels (2 -> 11): hydrogen, oxyhydrogen, coal gas, biogas, sour gas, coker gas, reform gas
- steam (3 -> 7): HBM's full steam ladder (spent, normal, hot, superhot, ultrahot at 0.1×/1×/2×/4×/8×)

## How values were picked

Real-world LHV × density for anything with a real analog (sources cited inline: Engineering Toolbox, Perry's, Gary & Handwerk, etc). For variants: hot = same as cold, leaded = same as unleaded, desulfurized = ~0.5–1% less, cracked/reformed adjusted for lighter/denser fractions respectively.

author: copilot
body:
No documentation existed explaining how to use the library's MXFP4 quantization and GEMM kernels, despite full implementations being present.

## Changes

- **`docs/tutorials/mxfp4_kernel.rst`** — New tutorial covering:
  - MXFP4 format internals (E2M1 elements, E8M0 block scales, `uint8` packing)
  - 3-stage pipeline: quantize → pre-shuffle → GEMM
  - High-level API (`aiter.gemm_a4w4`) and low-level Triton API (`gemm_afp4wfp4`)
  - Pre-shuffled weight path for inference throughput
  - Correctness verification against PyTorch reference via `fp4_utils`
  - Fused RMSNorm + MXFP4 quant (`fused_rms_mxfp4_quant`)
  - Batched GEMM (`batched_gemm_afp4wfp4`)
  - Architecture requirements (gfx950/CDNA4 for native HW support)
  - Complete `MXFP4Linear` module example

- **`docs/tutorials/index.rst`** — Added `mxfp4_kernel` to toctree and Advanced Topics list
- **`docs/index.rst`** — Added Quick Link to the new tutorial

## Example

```python
import aiter
from aiter.ops.shuffle import shuffle_weight

# Quantize weights once at load time (pre-shuffled)
quant_func = aiter.get_triton_quant(aiter.QuantType.per_1x32)
w_fp4, w_scales = quant_func(w_bf16, shuffle=True)
w_shuffled = shuffle_weight(w_fp4, layout=(16, 16))

# Per-token quantize activation + run GEMM
x_fp4, x_scales = quant_func(x, shuffle=True)
out = aiter.gemm_a4w4(x_fp4, w_shuffled, x_scales, w_scales, bpreshuffle=True)
```

author: airbagdeer
body:
Adds 5 PostgreSQL \`ltree\` operator filters to the v2 vector store metadata filtering system.

## Summary

Extends the MongoDB-style filter system with operators that map directly to PostgreSQL's built-in [\`ltree\`](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ltree.html) extension, enabling hierarchical path queries over tree-structured label data such as category taxonomies, org charts, and file paths.

## Motivation

In many retrieval system, a typical tree document system is implemented for order of files.
The existing filter system has no way to query \`ltree\`-typed columns or hierarchical path data stored in the JSON metadata column. Applications that classify documents with paths like \`Top.Science.Astronomy\` need ancestor/descendant traversal and pattern-matching that the \`ltree\` extension provides natively — none of which is expressible with \`\$eq\`, \`\$like\`, or the other existing operators.

## Changes

- **\`langchain_postgres/v2/async_vectorstore.py\`**: Added \`LTREE_OPERATORS\` constant, extended \`SUPPORTED_OPERATORS\`, and implemented the \`elif operator in LTREE_OPERATORS\` branch in \`_handle_field_filter\` with per-operator input validation and SQL generation
- **\`tests/unit_tests/fixtures/metadata_filtering_data.py\`**: Added \`LTREE_METADATAS\`, \`LTREE_FILTERING_TEST_CASES\` (12 cases), and \`LTREE_NEGATIVE_TEST_CASES\` (6 cases)
- **\`tests/unit_tests/v2/test_pg_vectorstore_search.py\`**: Added \`TestLtreeFiltering\` class with fixtures for both storage modes and 30 parametrized tests

## New Operators

| Operator | PostgreSQL | Description |
|---|---|---|
| \`\$ancestor\` | \`field @> CAST(val AS ltree)\` | Field is an ancestor of (or equal to) the value |
| \`\$descendant\` | \`field <@ CAST(val AS ltree)\` | Field is a descendant of (or equal to) the value |
| \`\$lquery\` | \`field ~ CAST(val AS lquery)\` | Field matches an lquery wildcard pattern |
| \`\$lquery_any\` | \`field ? ARRAY[...]\` | Field matches any pattern in a list of lqueries |
| \`\$ltxtquery\` | \`field @ CAST(val AS ltxtquery)\` | Field matches an ltxtquery full-text expression |

## Usage Examples

\`\`\`python
# \$ancestor — find categories that are on the path UP TO "Top.Science.Astronomy"
# ("Top" and "Top.Science" are ancestors of "Top.Science.Astronomy")
results = await vs.asimilarity_search(
    "query", filter={"category": {"\$ancestor": "Top.Science.Astronomy"}}
)

# \$descendant — find all documents under "Top.Science" (inclusive)
results = await vs.asimilarity_search(
    "query", filter={"category": {"\$descendant": "Top.Science"}}
)

# \$lquery — match direct children of Top only
results = await vs.asimilarity_search(
    "query", filter={"category": {"\$lquery": "Top.*{1}"}}
)

# \$lquery_any — match either of two exact paths
results = await vs.asimilarity_search(
    "query", filter={"category": {"\$lquery_any": ["Top.Science", "Top.Technology"]}}
)

# \$ltxtquery — match any path containing the label word "Science"
results = await vs.asimilarity_search(
    "query", filter={"category": {"\$ltxtquery": "Science"}}
)
\`\`\`

## Implementation Details

- Works with both **dedicated \`ltree\` columns** and **JSON-stored metadata** (the \`langchain_metadata\` JSONB column). For JSON fields, the \`->>\` extracted text is automatically cast to \`ltree\` before the operator is applied.
- Uses \`CAST(:param AS type)\` parameter syntax rather than \`:param::type\` to avoid a psycopg3 driver issue where \`::\` immediately following a named placeholder prevents parameter substitution.
- Requires the \`ltree\` PostgreSQL extension. The test fixtures call \`CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS ltree\`; the pgvector Docker image ships with it pre-installed.

## Test Coverage

- 12 positive test cases × 2 storage modes (dedicated \`ltree\` column + JSON metadata) = 24 passing tests
- 6 negative tests confirming that wrong value types raise \`ValueError\`
- All 44 existing metadata filter tests continue to pass — no regressions

## Breaking Changes

None — fully backward compatible.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added and passing (30 new + 44 regression)
- [x] Type hints correct (\`mypy\` clean)
- [x] Linting passes (\`ruff check\`, \`ruff format\`)
- [x] Spelling check passes (\`codespell\`)
- [x] No breaking changes

body:
Introduce arrival detection and UI plus multiple RouteDetail enhancements. Adds arrivedAtDest state, an effect that triggers when the user is within 300m of the destination, a dismissible "Du er fremme" banner, and resets arrival state when starting/stopping walks. Adjusts map stops rendering to respect expandedRoute and map centering logic.

In RouteDetail: import decodePolyline and add positionProgress to compute progress along a polyline from the user's location so active-leg progress can use real position when available. Improve platformLabel translations for various modes, show an in-minimized header message when riding transit (including get-off stop and time), raise proximity threshold used for detecting nearby stops, and derive platform labels from adjacent legs for transfer displays. These changes aim to improve arrival UX and make transit progress and platform info more accurate and informative.

#### 128fb92799f02173cf41a372e4e00c802cb99020 
[Site Isolation] Fix flaky ColorInputTests by waiting for color picker before setting color
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=310294
rdar://172931262

Reviewed by Aditya Keerthi.

The tests called _setSelectedColorForColorPicker: after a single waitForNextPresentationUpdate,
which is sometimes not enough time to guarantee that the ShowColorPicker IPC message has been
handled and internals().colorPicker is not null, due to recent site isolation work in this area.
When we hit the null check in didChooseColor() is hit, the color change is silently dropped,
causing us to read back the initial value #000000.

Spin the run loop until the WKPopoverColorWell appears in the view hierarchy before calling
_setSelectedColorForColorPicker:, matching the approach used by
UIScriptControllerMac::isShowingColorPicker.

This PR implements a comprehensive refactor of the frontend layer to improve maintainability, scalability, and adherence to modern React and Vercel best practices.

### Key Improvements:
1. **UI Logic Decoupling (Custom Hooks):** Business logic and state management have been extracted from core components into dedicated custom hooks (`useNavigation`, `useFiltersModal`, `useLanguageSelector`). This makes the UI components leaner and focused only on rendering.
2. **Project Structure Standardization:** Centralized all data models by migrating interfaces and types to `src/interfaces/` (using the `.interface.ts` suffix) and `src/types/`.
3. **Performance Optimization:** Applied Vercel's React best practices to optimize rendering cycles, specifically reducing the reliance on `useEffect` for derived state and improving component lifecycle management.
4. **UI Component Cleanup:** Significantly simplified complex components such as `FiltersModal.tsx`, reducing code complexity and improving readability.
5. **Pure Utility Extraction:** Moved generic logic (e.g. pagination) to pure utility functions in `src/utils/pagination.ts` for better testability.

author: copilot
body:
Implements a production-ready, self-recovering digital signage kiosk for Raspberry Pi 3/4 using a two-process architecture: a Node.js controller owning all reliability policy, and a Chromium kiosk renderer handling display.

## Controller (`controller/`)
- **State machine** — explicit `FALLBACK → PROBING_STREAM → STREAM` transitions, logged and event-driven
- **WS client** (`wsClient.js`) — connects to central server; handles `SET_STREAM_URL`, `CLEAR_STREAM`, `SET_FALLBACK_IMAGE`; exponential backoff + jitter reconnect
- **Renderer WS server** (`rendererServer.js`) — local `ws://127.0.0.1:8081` channel; queues commands when renderer not yet connected
- **Passive poller** (`passivePoller.js`) — optional HTTP endpoint polling when no active command stream; triggers same probe flow
- **Probe/retry policy** (`index.js`) — up to `maxStreamRetries` attempts with jitter delay before hard fallback; caches last working stream URL to `/var/lib/signage/last-stream.json`
- **Config** (`config.js`) — layered: system `/etc/signage/config.json` → `config/default.json` → env vars (all fields have `SIGNAGE_*` env overrides)
- **Logger** — Winston daily-rotate-file (5×10 MB), console transport; structured JSON fields

## Renderer (`renderer/`)
- Express static server on port 8080 serving a single-page kiosk app
- Probe runs in a hidden `<video>` element; only swaps opacity to visible after `PROBE_OK`
- HLS: native HLS where available, HLS.js CDN fallback otherwise
- Freeze detection: polls `currentTime` every 2 s; reports `PLAYBACK_FROZEN` after `freezeTimeoutMs` of no advance
- Smooth `opacity` transitions between fallback image and stream (no black flash)
- Reconnects to controller WS with backoff; maintains last visible state during disconnect

## Infrastructure
- `systemd/signage-controller.service` + `systemd/signage-kiosk.service` — `Restart=always`, correct `After=` ordering
- `scripts/install.sh` — creates dirs, installs deps, configures logrotate, enables services
- `scripts/start-kiosk.sh` — Chromium kiosk with Pi-appropriate flags (`--kiosk`, `--autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required`, `--noerrdialogs`, no first-run, no GPU sandbox)
- `README.md` — architecture diagrams, full config reference table, install steps, troubleshooting, acceptance checklist

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Build a production-ready Raspberry Pi digital signage kiosk client in this repository.

## Goal
Implement a lightweight, reliable, self-recovering signage client for Raspberry Pi 3/4 that:
- boots directly into fullscreen kiosk mode,
- shows a local fallback image by default,
- connects to a central server via WebSocket for control commands,
- plays a live stream only after playback is validated,
- automatically recovers from stream and network failures,
- remains stable with low CPU/memory usage.

## Repository
- owner/repo: BadSpider1/Signage
- base branch: main

## Required behavior

### 1) Startup
- On boot, launch automatically in fullscreen kiosk mode.
- Immediately show fallback image from local path (default `/opt/signage/default.jpg`).
- Keep fallback visible until stream is confirmed playable.

### 2) Server communication (WebSocket)
- Connect to configurable WebSocket server URL.
- Identify with unique `deviceId`.
- Handle commands:
  - `SET_STREAM_URL` (payload includes URL)
  - `CLEAR_STREAM`
  - `SET_FALLBACK_IMAGE` (payload includes local file path)
- Keep displaying last valid content during WS outages.
- Reconnect with exponential backoff + jitter.

### 3) Stream handling and validation
- Prefer HLS/compatible stream playback.
- Before switching to stream view, validate actual playback:
  - metadata loaded,
  - playback starts,
  - media time advances for at least a short interval.
- If validation fails, stay/return on fallback image.
- During runtime, detect freezes/crashes/disconnects quickly (target 5–10s).
- Retry stream startup with capped attempts; on repeated failure return to fallback.

### 4) Passive mode (optional stream discovery)
- If no active command stream, optionally poll a configured endpoint periodically.
- If endpoint indicates stream available, run validation then switch.
- If stream disappears, return to fallback immediately.

### 5) Performance constraints
- Raspberry Pi 3/4 friendly defaults.
- Keep UI simple (single page, minimal DOM updates).
- Avoid unnecessary re-renders.
- Ensure media pipeline uses platform/browser capabilities efficiently.

### 6) Display requirements
- True fullscreen kiosk behavior.
- No visible browser chrome, cursor, controls, debug overlays.
- Seamless transitions between fallback and stream (avoid black flashes where possible).

### 7) Logging and debugging
- Log key lifecycle events locally:
  - startup,
  - state transitions,
  - WS connect/disconnect/retry,
  - stream probe success/failure,
  - playback errors/freezes/recovery.
- Logs should be accessible on disk and not shown onscreen.
- Use basic log rotation or size protection to avoid disk growth.

## Implementation details

### Architecture
Implement two-process architecture:
1) **Controller (Node.js service)**
   - Owns state machine and reliability policy.
   - Handles WS connection/commands, passive polling, retries/backoff.
   - Exposes local control/status channel to renderer (localhost WebSocket or HTTP).
2) **Renderer (kiosk web app)**
   - Displays fallback image or stream fullscreen.
   - Performs stream probe/playback event reporting.
   - Contains no visible controls/UI.

### State machine
At minimum implement states:
- `FALLBACK`
- `PROBING_STREAM`
- `STREAM`

Transitions should be explicit and logged.

### Config
Provide config file + env override support with sensible defaults:
- `deviceId`
- `wsUrl`
- `fallbackImagePath` (default `/opt/signage/default.jpg`)
- `passiveEndpoint` (optional)
- `probeTimeoutMs` (default ~8000)
- `freezeTimeoutMs` (default ~6000)
- `maxStreamRetries` (default ~3)
- polling interval/backoff settings

Persist minimal runtime data (optional but recommended):
- last known working stream URL and timestamp.

### Kiosk boot/runtime
Include installation/run scripts and systemd units to launch on boot:
- Start controller service.
- Start kiosk browser pointing to local renderer URL.
- Include practical Chromium kiosk flags for Pi:
  - kiosk/app mode,
  - autoplay allowed,
  - no infobars/err dialogs,
  - no first-run prompts.
- Ensure restart-on-crash via systemd (`Restart=always`).

### Stream playback in renderer
- Implement robust video element lifecycle.
- HLS support strategy:
  - native HLS where available,
  - `hls.js` fallback when required and feasible.
- Probe stream in hidden/prep mode before visible switch.
- On runtime error/freeze, notify controller immediately.

### API/events between controller and renderer
Define a small internal protocol for actions and telemetry, e.g.:
- controller -> renderer:
  - `SHOW_FALLBACK` { path }
  - `PROBE_STREAM` { url, timeoutMs }
  - `PLAY_STREAM` { url }
  - `STOP_STREAM`
- renderer -> controller:
  - `PROBE_OK`
  - `PROBE_FAIL` { reason }
  - `PLAYBACK_ERROR` { reason }
  - `PLAYBACK_FROZEN`
  - periodic health heartbeat optional

1. Working code implementing above behavior.
2. `README.md` with:
   - architecture,

   - run/install instructions,
   - systemd...

## Summary

- Raise per-file test coverage for the compiled `UtilitiesCS/OutlookObjects/Folder` scope so every in-scope production file is verified at `>= 80%` line coverage.
- Add and expand deterministic MSTest coverage across the mirrored `UtilitiesCS.Test/OutlookObjects/Folder` suite, including a new `MAPIMethodsTests.cs` file and explicit `UtilitiesCS.Test.csproj` registration.
- Introduce narrowly scoped non-public seam hooks in `UtilitiesCS/OutlookObjects/Folder/FolderPredictor.cs` and `UtilitiesCS/OutlookObjects/Folder/FolderConverter.cs` so UI/filesystem-dependent branches can be exercised without live Outlook or manual prompts.

- Update the active feature documentation and evidence set under `docs/features/active/2026-03-19-outlook-folder-wrapper-tests-82/`, including archived audit artifacts and final QA gate records.

## Why

- `UtilitiesCS/OutlookObjects/Folder` contains wrapper, comparer, traversal, navigation, conversion, scoring, and prediction logic that is regression-prone when coverage is uneven or missing.

- `FolderPredictor.cs` and `FolderConverter.cs` were explicitly called out as harder-to-cover files because of tightly coupled UI/filesystem behavior, so the feature allows only minimal non-public seams where tests alone are insufficient.

body:
PullToOBS talks to OBS over WebSocket v5, starts recording the moment you enter combat, and saves a replay buffer clip of the prepull.

**AI Usage:** Copilot — I have programming experience, though not in C# or the Dalamud API specifically. I defined the requirements, made architectural and design decisions, reviewed all code for patterns and logic, and tested the plugin in-game. The C# and Dalamud-specific code was written by an AI assistant.

**Features**

- Starts OBS recording when combat begins, stops after a 5-second grace period
- Re-entering combat during grace period cancels the pending stop for continuous recording
- Saves replay buffer 5 seconds into the encounter to capture the prepull
- Visual on-screen indicator (red pulsing = recording, orange = replay buffer active, green = connected, grey = disconnected)
- Configure via `/pulltoobs` or `/pto`; toggle OBS connection with `/pto obs`

**Testing**

- Tested in-game with OBS WebSocket v5
- Verified recording starts/stops with combat transitions
- Verified replay buffer save on encounter start
- Verified grace period cancellation on combat re-entry

**Technical Details**

- Uses Dalamud Windowing API for all windows
- OBS calls run off the game thread (ThreadPool/kernel timers)
- No server interactions beyond OBS WebSocket

author: pacharanero
body:
## Summary

Switches the documentation toolchain from Material for MkDocs to [Zensical](https://zensical.com/), a drop-in replacement for MkDocs 1.x built by the Material for MkDocs team.

## Background

MkDocs 2.0 is a ground-up rewrite that is incompatible with Material for MkDocs - it removes plugin support, breaks the theming system, and has no migration path for existing projects. MkDocs 1.x is also effectively unmaintained. The Material for MkDocs team created Zensical specifically to provide a stable, long-term home for existing MkDocs projects. See: https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2026/02/18/mkdocs-2.0/

## Changes

- `requirements.txt` - replace `mkdocs-material` with `zensical`
- `mkdocs.yml` - switch to `variant: classic` theme, update emoji extension paths, update copyright year to 2026
- CI workflow - use `zensical` for install and deploy commands
- Docs - update references from MkDocs/Material to Zensical

Build validated locally with `zensical build --clean`.
